An example of what FTL would have been, if it was coded in 4 hours and then abandoned. Most tactical options are totally useless: game encourages you to build turrets on one side and everything else on another, but "doesn't know" about it, leading to manually routinely doing boring stuff. Seriously, do I have any single reason to not make everyone out of towers when doing "explore"? And moreover, if I didn't, then station is turned around to the side where warehouse (most "filler" building I have ever seen - zero cost, but you need to have one to collect anything), so people in turrets are locked and I need to wait another 30 seconds (on speed-up)  while couple of free persons will gather everything. If "return" button worked it would make it at least recoverable, but it simply stops your people from gathering resources, but trying to turn around station will still give "resources are being gathered" message.
Uselessness of choices is total: armories are useless, the whole idea of having two sides brings much more pain than interest, actually the only thing you need to build after you more-or-less set up civil side (workshop, tree, shield, tools, artifacts) are good turrets on another side. And for the most of the game your main concern will be "not forget to turn to offensive side and push people to turrets before flying, not forget to push people from turrets before gathering resources".
And for the most annoying part, making me ask for a refund, it is not even possible to save -- a complete showstopper for a game, for which taking out all special systems and checking if there is anything as a final one, can take more than half an hour.

I'll put it this way:  This game is free, has a story, and is pretty quick to get through.  There is really no real reason not to play it.  And I mean seriously, play this game.  I don't want my critiques to prevent anyone from trying it, but I do believe that any game has places where it can improve.
Some critiques:
-- Can't Run
(Not a game changer, but it would make it a little more convenient to get around, not to mention make it feel slightly more immersive)
-- Slightly Repetetive Gameplay
(You keep having to go upstairs over and over again to input stuff into a keyboard.  Not terrible, but it's not very interesting either.  This would'nt be as bad if going up and down the stairs wasn't as much of a chore with the game's lack of running)  There could have been various different kinds of locks or buttons for the player to press.
-- Confusion
(For example, there was not any clear indicator that I had entered the right password on the computer.  When it did make noises I thought it was rejected the password I had put in.  In fact for the longest time I didn't even realize that the keyboard was doing anything at all, and when I did the game was basically already over.  One thing that would help would be to turn the light on the keyboard green when you enter the right password, as well as have it output a sort of cheery "look you found a secret room" kind of noise.
-- Unclear/Unexplained Gameplay Mechanics
(With the keyboard being to vital to the gameplay there should have been some sort of clear explanation (a tutorial?) of what it's use was.  For example something could pop on screen, similar to when you first start the game, that tells the player how to use the computer.  This would more clearly imply that the keyboard is a recurring gameplay mechanic.  Additionally, there was never a single moment in the game that was like "hey!  that keyboard doesn't have any power!  Maybe I should turn on this generator over here.")
-- No Clear Objective
(As a player I felt less like I was accomplishing something and more like I was just wandering around randomly clicking on objects around the building.  In fact, having to go back to the keyboard made the game feel like I was never really progressing.  This of course would have been improved had I actually felt any reward from inputting the correct password into the keyboard, and remember, all that would need to be is an obvious green light and a positive noise.)
[In Summary]
Overall the game was a calm 30 minute experience with a decent story.  Given that this was free I feel not regrets for playing this game.  However, if it had cost money I would never reccomend this to anyone as the gameplay was not very good (albeit not terrible).
Suggestions for improvement:
-  Add the ability to run.
-  Make the keyboard feel more responsive.  **Not IRL Keyboard, In-Game Keyboard**
-  Make the individual objectives clearer.
-  Add variety to the way the players progress, or add a keyboard for every door.
-  Make the players feel more like they have actually made progress.

I think that Transistor is a great experience - visuals, music, dialogue, gameplay, they're all good! I especially had a lot of fun with the combat and skill combination system. The multitude of ways you can beat the crap out of your enemies makes mixing and matching skills/abilities very enjoyable. Adding the difficulty modifiers that you unlock as the game progresses make the encounters become much more engaging and rewarding.

First, the obvious: there are few games as beautiful as Transitor. I don't think I need to go into detail, since you can clearly see that on the store page. Transistor is also a very
game. It's active/modifier/passive system for abilities is extremely unique and engaging. At times it feels like you can use this to exploit the game, and so sometimes Transitor feels a bit too easy. I would suggest playing the game without retrying stages, at least after you have enough abilities to fall back on. If you do this, the game's difficulty is well calibrated: you amost always succeed, but it's often a very close call.
Now, as for the plot: it's thinner than you might guess. I was surprised to find that I was often rushed from one battle to the next without too much of an intermission. Luckily, the combat is fun enough that this wasn't really a fualt. Transistor is a piece of art, and like so much great art, Transistor's meaning is vague, even at he end. The story is not confusing or empty, certainly: the game gives you content to mentally fidget with, and time to do so, but it never outright tells (or shows) you exactly what's going on. Transistor rewards players for expirimenting with their loadouts by granting little chunks of lore, which I felt was a nice bridge between the gameplay and the world-building parts of the experience. In every aspect Transistor is enjoyable, but those expecting an existential masterpiece may be disappointed.

This is a review for people who have this game in their backlog.  It's not a review of this game as it was when released in 2014 but a review of me playing it in 2016.
Overall: 9/10.  I've previously played Bastion by the same publisher, and I have to say the plot feels kind of recycled.  You play a mute protagonist who is narrated by a smooth talking deep male voice from off-screen.  Along the way you are realizing that some awful fate has befallen your city.  The world is nearly empty except for you and two or three other voices.  You need to find out why.  The plot is good and well realized, there aren't any gaping holes and the environments are engagng.
Graphics: 10/10.  It's not a AAA game.  It's not trying to be.  It has hand-painted art-deco backgrounds that are absolutely gorgeous in isometric view.  The particle effects are crisp and clean and communicate exactly what will happen to your character.  The cut scenes are beautiful and from a perspective that cleanly shows you what you should be looking at.  I think the encroaching sterility of the world in this game is better reflected than the blight in Bastion, and I'll give the art direction full marks because of that.
Sound: 9/10. I bought the soundtrack and have it loaded into my car's MP3 Shuffle.  Some of the combat effects could have used diversity. The voice acting is a delight, but some of the dialogue lines are repetitive without having value to their replication.  I think the voice acting in Bastion was better, but the soundtrack in this game is better realized.  Both are ultimately a delight.
Gameplay: 10/10, perhaps even better.  It's a tactical action RPG hybrid beatemup.  There must be thousands of loadout combinations for your character's abilities, and the way that your items interact is so enjoyable you almost want to spend more time in the sandbox than in the real game.  The plot comes out of using your abilities, and not out of progressing through the world, which is an interesting twist to engage a generation that doesn't necessarily want to endlessly scroll through dialogue in cut-scenes.  Each of the game's 20 or so abilities has an Active, a Modifier and a Passive component.  For example, there is an active to ()Crash that is a melee sword strike, a modifier that lets you pair it with another ability to make that ability better early in a combo, and a passive component that gives tankiness.  You are not instructed to use any particular component, but you find your own playstyle.  It's a good discovery.
The beatemup component of the game is crisp, with good controls on both keyboard and mouse (which I preferred) and controller.  The directional pathing is responsive and enjoyable.  Load scenes are non-existent.
The tactical component feels thoroughly challenging.  You either play aggressively in tactics and passively in beatemup or you play a character designed for beatemup and then move to a tactical overlay for assassinations.  It really feels like this game shines with both modes in a way that neither one would contribute.
Even two years in, this format is refreshing and has not been replicated in any game I've played.
Replayability; 9/10.  The plot and sense of discovery thoroughly drives the game.  You'll lose something on the replay in New Game ++ that you had during the first playthough.  Also, to me, the game was unbelievably hard in the New Game ++ mode compared to the original mode.  In the original mode, on player defeat you lose combat abilities for a set time, and this allows you to fight for your life to keep going.  In New Game ++ the enemies are remarkably tough TACTICALLY without a boost to just raw stats.  This makes defeats incredibly punishing and the game very challenging.  I enjoyed New Game ++ from what I played of it, but I'm not skilled enough to beat it.  I think others might find the difficulty a bit more rewarding over the original format, which may have actually been a tad too easy.

Voxelized: A game which is seemingly (read heavily) inspired by famous "block builder" Minecraft. The game is currently in it's Early Access stage, and unfortuately shows that the "Early" in early access, means "The beginning."  At the time of writing this review, there seems to be nothing noteworthy about the game.  Here's a little bit of info on gameplay.
There are two levels right now, however only one of them seems to be accessible: The first level is a typical mountain-esque level. There are blocks all around, and seem to be in a hill/mountain shape. By left-clicking you can remove a block. By right clicking, you can add a block. The game, however, does not tell you that you have to pause the game (With the escape button, also not stated in the game) and select on the left side of your screen a number from 0 to 23 (I've read others have been able to get 25, I myself, cannot.) With the number selected, you will create a different block with your right click. The 24 (or 25?) blocks are mostly unique in color, and a few of them are even unique in design; There's a door frame block, and an invisble glass-looking block. You can explore, create, and delete to your hearts content. However at the moment that's all there is to do.
The second level, however, has not been able to load for me. From the picture it shows at the level select screen, it seems to be just a plain open field, which might be better for those of you that would like a flat landscape to create your dream block-thingy on.
For the feature available in the game, they work great. I've had no issues deleting, or creating blocks. The jumping physics seem to work well too. All in all, this might just be a game you should wait until is finished to purchase and play. At the moment, I don't find it worth even what it costs, or even at the coupon price you might have.

This game is simply fantastic.
After first hearing of this game I wasn't all that excited about it so I ignored it. However now, a few years after release I think to myself how foolish I was underestimating this game and it's potential.
So I will talk about this game a bit without spoiling it for you guys.
So you're playing as the character Wei who is a undercover agent trying to end the Triad activity in his home town (Hong Kong) as he gets into the Triad gang he slowly makes his way into the hierarchy whilst still being undercover gaining their trust etc. In the game there are numerous occasions where you have to beat the hell out of a bunch of Triad members from different gangs whilst helping your gang and helping the police. As you play the more difficult things get for you and you get into even more struggle.
The thing about this game which makes it so damn fun, is how it's a game where instead of using your common guns like you do in (For example: Grand Theft Auto Series) you actually mostly use Wei's insane martial art skills which you get better in the more you play as you are able to unlock different fighting techniques. So the game focuses more about fighting than guns which may sound weak and boring, in my opinion it's a lot more fun than your typical "Go there, shoot him, chase him, shoot him and drive back" type of game. And I'm not even saying gun fights are bad in this, they're actually also a crap tonn of fun when there's a gun fight as you don't expect it at all when it happens and then it's just badass! Two rival triad gangs batteling against eachother. So, it's not all just fists and kicks. It's a mix between guns and fighting. (approx. 80% fighting 20% shooting)
And you don't just have to do those undercover missions because there are also side jobs which involve you either racing, busting drug deals, leading investigations about different cases and also missions which involve you helping the public allowing you to buy more things throughout the map. Also there's approx 16 hours of main mission gameplay (I might have played a few side jobs in those 16 hours. I'm still doing most of the side jobs and after going to play the 2 DLC's) so as you can see you can have a lot of fun for a long time. Also there's a few collectable items scattered around the map if you're into treasure hunting.
Also my favorite thing about this game is: In most areas around the map you can use the enviroment to your advantage. For example: You can throw someone in head first into a branch cutter.
These are now my ratings out of 10:
-Story: 7/10
-Graphics: 6.5/10
-Entertainment: 8.5/10
-Difficulty (10 being hardest): 6/10
Pros
------
1. God damn great fighting.
2. Very immersive and interesting story.
3. Funny a lot of the times (if you have a sick humour like me :D)
4. Good graphics.
5. A big variety of different cars.
6. Clothing customization (You can be dressed as some kind of golden statue and that gives you 60% melee defense.)
7. Fun side jobs.
Cons.
------
1. You can't keep the weapons/guns you picked up either from the map or during a mission.
2. Fighting is too easy. (It's still really fun beating the sh!t out of others)
3. You can't start a havoc in the city like you can in GTA with guns and mass murder, instead you are forced to run around town drop kicking everyone which is always still fun.
(Those are the legit 3 things I can think of which I didn't really like about the game)

So the time has come to write a review about my most treasured game from the old Amiga 500-era. I played it as a kid and I was fascinated by the atmosphere the game was able to create. Lost Patrol on the Amiga 500 was also a game that fascinated me due to the tense atmosphere. But Wings back then was a better game because of the dogfights in 3D-graphic it had to offer. When I saw the remastered version of Wings last year in a store I felt immediately atracted to the idea that they could have brought this wonderful (partly fictional partly real) story to modern PCs.
To fully understand why I give the game a thumb down, first I feel the duty to write down the pros and cons of the "old" Amiga 500 Version.
Pros: - For that time in the 90ies stunning 3D-graphic (sky-dogfights)
- Music and overall-art fits perfectly to the 1916-1918 years where the game takes place
- Captivating squadron-diary that made the game feel alive
- Dogfights had a kind of soul to it because of content of the diary and short text introduction to the mision
- You could distribute points for improvement of your planes quality (Shooting, Flying abilities, etc.)
- Strafe and bombing misions gave the game a good variation and was fun to play
Cons: - After many hours the music was irritating
So now to the actual remastered version of the game WINGS. But first let me type down that Cinemaware the studio which is responsible for the remastered version also is the studio from the original version in the 90ies. They had a kickstarter-campaign for the game but the goal werent achieved so they worked on a plan to size the expectations down. They tried another kickstarter campaign in 2013 with a lower goal. They were able to get 85.000 Dollars for the game so that the kickstarter-campaign was successful. They worked then on the game, and then in late 2014 they started selling the game.
And why do I write all this? Because that is exactly what you are going to get: A downsized game that had to clash with reality and confronted lowered expectations. I am really a die-hard WINGS-Fan and here you have the pros and cons of the remastered version
- Pros: - Good music. They took the old notes and recorded nice soundpieces in a good quality. Overall sound is satisfying. Specially if you compare to old Amiga 500 version.
- Narrator. A feature that the old version hadnt. You can turn the narration off in options.
- The dogfights are fun to play even with that simplicity and repetitiveness it offers. The immersion is good.
- Interface (various languages)
- Cons: - The graphics are not up-to-date and they are not at the same height as the soundquality.
- There are elements missing in this game: You see anti-aircraft fire exploding in the air in nearly every mision, but when you fly nearer to the ground all you can see are trees and houses in poor detailed graphic. I played one mision where I had to shoot spy-ballons. There I saw anti-aircraft canons on the ground. Why not in every mision? It is absurd to see aa-fire exploding all around you but below you: Nothing! The source cant be found!
- Dont let the third Steam-Picture fool you. There are no red enemy planes that you have to eliminate! (And I played the game until April 1917, when the Richthofen-Geschwader should already be present with their  red painted fokkers in every dogfight)
- There isnt a third-person "enemy hunts you" camera perspective where you have to try to shake the enemy off your tail. It appears only one time for 3 seconds  before a dogfight (in March 1917) starts. It says "Alright Fritz, lets see what you have got!". And thats all for the cinematic-scenes in this remastered version. Its a rip off! You will find yourself frustrating after you find out that you cant control your plane. 3 seconds of what? Showing that you have begun a task that you never finished? There are poorer young programmers living in their parents home that would have programed this remastered version with more enthusiasm and with less dollars in their eyes.
- The pilot still looking for enemy planes although his plane is on fire and heading for a probably deadly crash to ground? Seriously? I know that this was also this way in old-version of the game, but they could have changed that. It just looks so absurd and unreal! Its like a guy attacks you with a Katana from the front while you know that but still look at the bees behind you that might come to attack you.
- The AI specially of friendly plane units should be improved.
- I often saw friendly planes flying in the exact same spot, like a glitch without collision detection, not crashing though
- The pre-dogfight text often has nothing to do with what you encounter later in the mision. For example: "We were about to surprise 8 biplanes coming closer to their tails. It seems that we had all the advantages, but considering that they outnumbered us, even this situation looked like loosing for us!" Then in the mision you start as always (!!!) having your enemy coming nearer in front of you in a head to head- situation. Seriously? Is that what the developers owe to the once great game WINGS?
- The enemy planes always go down the same manner. While you can still fly one tumbling direction when your motor is on fire and black smoke fills the air. The enemy will always dive straight to the ground without signs that he could try an emergency landing like you can.
- Why is it still not posible to make a full upward looping, to then come down and attacking from the sun?
- You can loose all your progress with one pilot if you die and then push the NO-button when the program asks you to start from the last automatically saved-game (you cant save individually). What? At least the game could give some kind of  warning that I will loose  the pilot completely and that the profile of the pilot will be forever death in the memories-section. I played over 100 missions and had over 200 dogfight kills (I played until April 1917) and then: BOOM! In your face! Your profile is deleted and gone forever! Do you want to start in 1916 again and play again 20 hours? Or do you want to continue as a greenhorn in 1917 with Waldo P. Barnstormer and a kamikaze-suicide-plane against the fully equiped Jagdgeschwader? Grrrrrrr.Very upsetting.
So thats all. I think the Wings- Fans should have received a finished product instead of delivering half-baked Nostalgia of what once was a finished and perfect game. If the game had been done right, they could have created a new fan-base. The story of Wings, the immersion, the overall atmosphere and historical content with value surely would have captivated a lot more people. The game deserves a much better version. Somewhere I read that the developers are planning a directors cut version after this remastered edition.
Only thing that I have left to say is that many gamers are tired of publishers publishing unfinished games. And the developers should not be the ones to take all the blame on their shoulders. Yet they would have delivered a better version of WINGS if they had more enthusiasm and less moneymaking in mind. And I am absolute certain about this.

Spoiler free review.
I like this game more than gta-series. Mainly because it has more serious story. Gta is fun, but i just personally prefer more serious approach. The story tells of an undercover cop, infiltrating and destroying a triad organization from within, but eventually, he becomes friends with them, and starts to notice, they might not be as bad as he thought. They're just humans, with relationship, and hardships in life that drove them to the criminal path.
I really liked this aspect, it wasn't the basic "good guys are good guys, and bad guys are bad guys" type of setting. It was an interesting plot to follow.
The city itself is lively, fun to explore, parkour aspect contributes to the joy of exploring, and gives new areas where to go. Sidequests are plenty, helping people, learning new martial art moves and hunting for collectibles. There's also police missions, in addition to the triad ones. But it seems they didn't really explore how they wuold collide, like really give a hint that you're on the danger of revealing yourself to the triad during the police missions.
------------------The DLC-------------------------
Definitive edition comes with all of them, of course. The first being integrate into the game, the zodiac tournament, is a fun little nod to Bruce Lee, and the one i found most enjoyable of the 3 biggest story dlc's.
Nightmare in North Point is a horror themed, little and short dlc set only in North point, not much story. My second favorite of these ones.
The last one, year of the snake continues from the main story, basically for the intro video. It was a big letdown, i mean a BIG. After the intro video, it's just mainly cop missions from the main game, put one after atnoher, and after few of them, it's done. That's it. There's some minor story dialoque in some "missions", when Wei is driving a car and talking on the phone for example. It seemed to me, that it was putten together hastily. When Zodiac tournament and Nightmare had more proper feel to them.

On it's surface it's a pretty straight-forward beat'em up- that much is a given. But there are enough times where it subverts the genre that elevates this game to something else. The levels are relatively smooth as far as progression and learning the game. The boss fights at the end of each stage go from clever to insane. But, it's also subversive to the beat'em up genre. Mid-late in the game there is a stage where you get guns. A complete abundance of guns. It's only a moment, but in that moment you feel overpowered. But in the best way, because it doesn't last. It's a great peak for the game though, it makes sense storywise, and it really pushes things forward.

The only negative thing I can say about this game are the arenas. There is a base mechanic of the game that involves injecting/scouring chems. And to upgrade the chem you can use you have to beat a 10-wave arena. There are like 8-10 chems outside of the base chem you start with, each earned by beating a 10-wave arena. But you can beat the game with the basic chem. And the arenas are pretty tough. So, the arenas aren't really worth it. Which is a shame, because they can be pretty fun if you just want to beat enemies down.
Overall, I'd recommend Mother Russia Bleeds.

A nicely disturbing but meditative experience. FIngerbones is a mood and story driven game, where you discover the horrying nature of your character and the meaning behind "fingerbones" the deeper you explore your bunker. The puzzles are few, and not incredibly difficult, but require you to pay attention to the bits and pieces of plot that you discover through notes or your character's musings. The plot is well-written and the visuals are well-rendered. The atmosphere is incredibly eerie. One particular aspect of the atmosphere I really enjoyed was present in the main room of the game. You can clearly tell the sun is setting on the outside because the light that sneaks in through the few window shines an orange glow on the room. Moreover, the room appears to not have been open in months, because it is filled with dust particles up to the ceiling. This combination makes up for a really grabbing atmosphere for first few minutes of gameplay. Disturbingly surreal.

I could maybe defend this decision if the rest of the game were an exercise in cold dread. Instead it's a collection of adventure game tropes. You will plod around a small set of rooms, receiving passwords for free by clicking on little notes.
At one point it may appear that the game has left something to your imagination. If you want to salvage some value from the time you invested, this is when you should leave the building. In fact just about any early exit from the game will leave you with lingering questions more interesting than the hamhanded ending and its inappropriate, childish epilogue.

I think that Transistor is a great experience - visuals, music, dialogue, gameplay, they're all good! I especially had a lot of fun with the combat and skill combination system. The multitude of ways you can beat the crap out of your enemies makes mixing and matching skills/abilities very enjoyable. Adding the difficulty modifiers that you unlock as the game progresses make the encounters become much more engaging and rewarding.

First, the obvious: there are few games as beautiful as Transitor. I don't think I need to go into detail, since you can clearly see that on the store page. Transistor is also a very
game. It's active/modifier/passive system for abilities is extremely unique and engaging. At times it feels like you can use this to exploit the game, and so sometimes Transitor feels a bit too easy. I would suggest playing the game without retrying stages, at least after you have enough abilities to fall back on. If you do this, the game's difficulty is well calibrated: you amost always succeed, but it's often a very close call.
Now, as for the plot: it's thinner than you might guess. I was surprised to find that I was often rushed from one battle to the next without too much of an intermission. Luckily, the combat is fun enough that this wasn't really a fualt. Transistor is a piece of art, and like so much great art, Transistor's meaning is vague, even at he end. The story is not confusing or empty, certainly: the game gives you content to mentally fidget with, and time to do so, but it never outright tells (or shows) you exactly what's going on. Transistor rewards players for expirimenting with their loadouts by granting little chunks of lore, which I felt was a nice bridge between the gameplay and the world-building parts of the experience. In every aspect Transistor is enjoyable, but those expecting an existential masterpiece may be disappointed.

This is a review for people who have this game in their backlog.  It's not a review of this game as it was when released in 2014 but a review of me playing it in 2016.
Overall: 9/10.  I've previously played Bastion by the same publisher, and I have to say the plot feels kind of recycled.  You play a mute protagonist who is narrated by a smooth talking deep male voice from off-screen.  Along the way you are realizing that some awful fate has befallen your city.  The world is nearly empty except for you and two or three other voices.  You need to find out why.  The plot is good and well realized, there aren't any gaping holes and the environments are engagng.
Graphics: 10/10.  It's not a AAA game.  It's not trying to be.  It has hand-painted art-deco backgrounds that are absolutely gorgeous in isometric view.  The particle effects are crisp and clean and communicate exactly what will happen to your character.  The cut scenes are beautiful and from a perspective that cleanly shows you what you should be looking at.  I think the encroaching sterility of the world in this game is better reflected than the blight in Bastion, and I'll give the art direction full marks because of that.
Sound: 9/10. I bought the soundtrack and have it loaded into my car's MP3 Shuffle.  Some of the combat effects could have used diversity. The voice acting is a delight, but some of the dialogue lines are repetitive without having value to their replication.  I think the voice acting in Bastion was better, but the soundtrack in this game is better realized.  Both are ultimately a delight.
Gameplay: 10/10, perhaps even better.  It's a tactical action RPG hybrid beatemup.  There must be thousands of loadout combinations for your character's abilities, and the way that your items interact is so enjoyable you almost want to spend more time in the sandbox than in the real game.  The plot comes out of using your abilities, and not out of progressing through the world, which is an interesting twist to engage a generation that doesn't necessarily want to endlessly scroll through dialogue in cut-scenes.  Each of the game's 20 or so abilities has an Active, a Modifier and a Passive component.  For example, there is an active to ()Crash that is a melee sword strike, a modifier that lets you pair it with another ability to make that ability better early in a combo, and a passive component that gives tankiness.  You are not instructed to use any particular component, but you find your own playstyle.  It's a good discovery.
The beatemup component of the game is crisp, with good controls on both keyboard and mouse (which I preferred) and controller.  The directional pathing is responsive and enjoyable.  Load scenes are non-existent.
The tactical component feels thoroughly challenging.  You either play aggressively in tactics and passively in beatemup or you play a character designed for beatemup and then move to a tactical overlay for assassinations.  It really feels like this game shines with both modes in a way that neither one would contribute.
Even two years in, this format is refreshing and has not been replicated in any game I've played.
Replayability; 9/10.  The plot and sense of discovery thoroughly drives the game.  You'll lose something on the replay in New Game ++ that you had during the first playthough.  Also, to me, the game was unbelievably hard in the New Game ++ mode compared to the original mode.  In the original mode, on player defeat you lose combat abilities for a set time, and this allows you to fight for your life to keep going.  In New Game ++ the enemies are remarkably tough TACTICALLY without a boost to just raw stats.  This makes defeats incredibly punishing and the game very challenging.  I enjoyed New Game ++ from what I played of it, but I'm not skilled enough to beat it.  I think others might find the difficulty a bit more rewarding over the original format, which may have actually been a tad too easy.

I'd been waiting to write a review for this game until I had played through the whole thing, but then got sucked into the expansion. As a little background, I'm an experienced MMO player and a leader in an online gaming community. I won't bore you with the exhaustive list of MMOs I've played, but we've been around and seen what the genre has to offer!
For those who prefer a TLDR, here it is:
-FFXIV is one of the best MMOs I've ever played, even taking into account the sub fee. The level of content support for this game is also on an entirely different level. Don't hesitate to download the trial and try it out!  Just remember the challenge comes as you get further in!
For those who prefer a thorough breakdown of strengths and weaknesses, including all major aspects of the game, read on!  I will break this down as succinctly as I can, but bear with me, because this game is unbelievably massive in terms of content vs. age.
*Disclaimer* This game is a Story Driven MMORPG. If you don't enjoy reading through the main scenario quests or watching any of the many cutscenes, you can certainly find content that is to your liking, but you will be playing only a portion of the game and missing some of the best parts. While it does start out slow, I promise the story evolves into one of the best MMO stories I've ever played, excepting perhaps Star Wars: The Old Republic.
Pro's:
-Excellent Story that will engage you and make the world come to life. Especially once you get nearer to the first expansion.
-Best Class System of ANY MMO. One character can separately level any or ALL classes in the game. No needing a new character to try out a different class. You can switch on the fly at any time outside dungeons and not in combat, complete with saved gear for that class spec. Special inventory for armor also eliminates the impact of this system on your character for needing to carry XX sets of gear. Cross-class abilities give you a good reason to level additional classes without it being mandatory.
-Exquisite Musical Scores. No, really. Final Fantasy is known for delivering moving music, but they outdid themselves on many of the scores in this game. Especially in the expansion. I have found myself just standing there and listening in-game without intending to.
-Most Impressive Crafting System in Any MMO. I know this is an easy claim to make and a hard one to back up, but crafting in this game IS a game of it's own. Providing all details of the crafting system would take an entire review of its own, so I'll try to hit the highlights. Crafting can matter! The older crafting content is useful for new players, cross class leveling for existing players, and cosmetic appearance that allows you to overlay one piece of gear with the look of another (the cosmetic crafted gear is some of the best looking gear in the game). New content is often nearly as powerful as current endgame gear, and is EXCEEDINGLY challenging to make. You also have things to make such as buffs and housing items for the public housing systems to show off in your guild house and/or neighborhood.
-Graphics. This is one of the few MMOs that can be played in 4K. Although it was designed for lower resolutions, you definitely notice a major difference. Even without 4k, the game is stunning. Well designed environments full of content truly immerse you in the world.
-The Amount of Content. Flat. Out. Massive. This game has 14 large areas that stay relevant throughout your experience of playing the game. Even after completing the game, those areas are useful for finding rare monsters (Hunts) that reward you with current tier tokens for gear (which are always kept current). It also has 3 major cities and a theme park (more on that next). The scale of all the quests and content that can be explored is amazing and will keep exploration player types busy for a long time. Add to that a total of 21 dungeons, and 10 Hard Mode variations, and it's quite daunting for completionists. As an aside, those hard modes are complete reworks of the originals with different layouts new enemies and their own stories, not just a rehash of the originals like so many games use. Did I mention 20 Raids, and 27 Trials (Raid-like single boss fights)? Oh, and this is just a review for the base game, so that is NOT counting all the content in the expansion!
-Do you like Minigames? Beware this game, because you'll forget to play the rest of it. The Gold Saucer (Theme Park from FFVII) has a number of quick minigames, a regular appearance of special activities, Chocobo Racing, a game-wide collectable card game with regular tournaments, a weekly lottery, and even an RTS game (similar to StarCraft/Warcraft, though not as complex) you play using your minions (cosmetic pets earned from many places in the game). The chocobo racing even has it's own leveling system for your race chocobos AND a breeding system to raise new birds. The collectable card game can be played with MANY NPC's throughout the rest of the game and around the world. They are all multiplayer compatable.
-Gameplay. While some classes do have similarities, mostly they all play very differently to one another. Black mages go from burning all their mana on damaging fire cycles to regenerating it a super speed on Ice cycles. Dark Knights balance a similar process, but it revolves around offensive vs. defensive capabilities while tanking. Astrologians search for the best beneficial temporary buffs while keeping up with healing. This combined with more challenging content later in the game in dungeons and raids (and optional extra difficult versions) keeps you engaged at any skill level.
Cons:
-Inventory. While the robust class system is supported by your special inventory for gear (your Armoury), there are an insane number of items in this game. Especially for crafters/gatherers. They have said there are plans in the works to improve this issue with the next expansion, Stormblood, in Summer 2017, but meanwhile, this remains one of the biggest daily irritations in the game. If you don't craft or harvest, you probably won't care much.
-Bots. I'm only listing this here because, not long ago, the amount of spam tells you would receive was horrible.  However, they recently put an additional system in to allow people to report RMT spammers as soon as one person receives a /tell. This is used to quickly lock out spamming accounts. I went from dozens of spam tells over a couple hours of play to maybe one a week.  ...Maybe. This issue is solved.
-PvP. They DO have PvP. However, it's not the best PvP I've ever played. It's not the worst, either, and they do put a lot of effort in to try to keep classes balanced with how their abilities work in PvP and have continuing tournaments all the time with new scenarios/maps on an infrequent basis. However, I didn't find it interesting, and I usually love PvP. I will give them points for making sure PvP balance does NOT affect PvE content. Your abilities have different uses in PvP content.  This has been a huge issue in some other games.
-Lack of Early Grouping Content. This is NOT a game that you can jump in and do a lot of content with your friends. Until about level 15 in the Main Scenario quests, about the only content you can group with your friends for is FATES (a public quest system) and sidequests. However, if you spend all your time grouping in those, you'll level well, but not unlock any content, since nearly evrything is unlocked via the Main Story quests, including higher level dungeons (since all dungeons are part of the story). This can be a turn-off for many new players with gaming buddies already playing. My advice is stick with it and just do Main Story quests while your friends make you some gear for level 20+. ;-)
That about covers the highlights of the Pro's and Con's. I will try to respond to any questions regarding particular aspects of the game in the comments.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

The game modes are fun. Titan Mode is the main game mode, where you protect your Titan and power it up between phases. Again, this is a mode made for team tactics, but no one communicates. This one is an interesting one indeed. Basic premise of the game is thus; you're a space faring fortress, on a mission to eradicate a virus of some sort (which I only learned from the game over screen, har de har.). You cruise around the galaxy visiting stars which either contain resources (resource gathering, management), settlements which must be attacked and defeated (tower defence time, ya'll.) in order to claim their resources, and finally stores, which allow you to buy extra resources, repair kits etc., or repair stations that allow you to repair and upgrade your towers. This continues until you have a force capable of taking on a-la 'boss' settlements.
So.
The game is pretty fun, in a play windowed whilst watching YouTube in the backround sort of way. The graphics are simple and unoffensivce. The soundtrack is surprisingly fitting and unobtrusive, given the price tag. The gameplay is very happy clicky don't think too hard sort of fare.
However.
It needs work. It be a little buggy, occasionally you'll begin a new game, and resource platforms won't load in. Speeding up time (which allows your little minions to collect resources, fight, etc. quicker) often causes your citizens to run backwards and forwards helplessly. But nothing that won't be easily fixed, I suppose.
There really isn't a whole lot of content. It's going to get old really fast without a stream of updates adding more stuffings.
There isn't a save feature. This needs sorted. I can't sugar coat it.
However.
I got this for eighty pence. You may as well give it a shot.
Also, click the flag on the lower right of the title screen, unless you can read Russian ;)

This is a very fun game, and well worth the cost. I finished the game in both easy and hard modes, and it can certainly be done despite there being no save game option.
I have left a lot of feedback that I think can improve the game, and the dev has been responsive.
I have high hopes that this game will be great in future. Right now it's good, but it has a ton of potential.
There's a lot of randomness in the game, which I think makes it more fun. Fuel isn't a problem, but it's definitely tough to balance the other resources.
I found it's best to explore a bit at the start, and then complete the mission. First time I played, I explored a ton at the start, but that made the late game very tricky as the number of enemies you fight seems to be related to the number of times you've moved since the start of the game. If this is balanced a bit more, then you can easily use multiple strategies. For now, especially considering the lack of a save game feature, playing quickly is definitely best!
It's certainly an interesting combination of turn based and realtime strategy, plus of course there's some tower defense elements. There's no mazing involved, but there's several types of turrets that can be levelled up.
Overall, I certainly recommend this game.

I have played many great games... tf2, counterstrike, skyrim, deadspace, bioshock, grand theft auto, far cry, resident evil, fallout, left 4 dead, borderlands, battlefield, portal, half-life.. I could go on and on... many of these games, I played and finished all the objectives, and even replayed them several times,  but no game has ever lasted on me as long as this game has. I have been playing this game for 14 years to today. That alone should be a testament to how great this game is.  And look around the reviews, I am not the only one who has been playing this game for this long, this game has been around for more than 2 decades and is kept alive by its devoted community, who have worked hard to maintain the servers, and keep the place hacker free.
Subspace Continuum is a 2D space online multiplayer game. While population declined a bit over the last years, there have been servers that supported 200 people simultaneously playing in a huge map, without lag being an issue.
Controls are easy to learn, but it may take a couple of hours to get used to the physics, depending on your experience playing space games(2d). Once you do though, flying becomes second nature to you and you can focus on the objectives at hand. There are many 'zones' (servers) to pick from. Each with a different flavor, and a different sub-community, and even different physics settings! I recommend giving a few of them a try, until you find the one that works for you, and stick to that one!
The chat system is hands down, the best I have seen in any game. It has public, team, private, group, squad messaging, to name a few. I think that chat system alone takes the game to a whole new level, as many of todays games purposely make chats impersonal by making room for just 1 very crowded chat room, with limited ability to scroll through them, or look back at conversations.
The different spaceships, cater to different playstyles. There are ships that move fast, there are ships that can take a punch, there are ships that shoot fast, or quickly, there are others that are there to support other ships. You are bound to find one that works for you.
Different zones hold different game modes. In some zones you have to protect something, or hold it in your teams possession for a given amount of time, in others you are just there to fight and eliminate the enemy. Regardless of which zone you choose, subspace is a game that you can just join, and play anytime of day.
All in all, I think this game deserves an honest shot from everyone. It has been around for more than twenty years and is still alive for a very good reason, it is addicting, it is fun, and it is worth downloading and trying out.

There's nothing like a good old fashioned beat 'em up, and that's just what you get with Mother Russia Bleeds.
Of course there's a bit more to it then that. The game is set in an alternate history Russia, where the government has seized control of just about everything and rules with an iron fist. You control one of four characters taking part in a fighting ring, who afterwards are kidnapped by government forces and experimented on. You wake up, having become totally dependent on a new drug called Nekro. You battle your way out of the facility you were imprisoned in, and set out to find out who is responsible for what was done to you, and in the process topple the corrupt government regime.
Although it sounds like an exciting story, and while the writing is solid, the story is not the strongest point of the game. That would be the look, the sound, and the intense gameplay itself. The graphics, as you can see in the trailers and photos, are very 16-bit and retro inspired. It serves the astentic of the game well, and feels like you're playing on the SNES or Genesis. Partnered with the excellent soundtrack, you definately won't be bored with the look or the sound of the game while playing.
But it all comes down to how it plays, and it plays wonderfully. The four characters all have different stats, just like you'd find in an old school game like Streets of Rage or Final Fight. One character is fast but weak, one is slow but strong, with two others having stats somewhere in the middle. You can punch, kick, throw some combos, grab and toss enemies, grab enemies and hit them repeatedly, or simply slam them into the ground. You can also use the drug you're addicted to, Nekro, to either refill health or enter a berserk rage type of mode. Defeated enemies will sometimes convulse on the ground, which allows you to stick a syringe in them and refill the Nekro for repeated use. You also get a wide variety of weapons, from poles, clubs, helmets, and knives, to even pistols and rifles with limited ammo.
The best part of it all is the gore, as defeated enemies will seep blood, and crushed heads with leave a gooey paste on the floor. Your campaign of murder can be played by yourself, or with four player local co-op (no online, which is a bummer). There are eight levels, with three difficulty settings, with a bit of a difficulty spike in the last two. You also end up with an arena mode where you battle hordes of enemies, trying to reach the 10th wave to unlock new strains of Nekro for use. Couple all of this with the achievements, and you have an excellent package with a lot of replay value.
In Soviet Russia, game buys you. So go and play it now comrade!

This game is so good that I am actually going to take the time to review it. Which I have never done before.
First of all, it is absolutely free. No in game charges, no pay to play, nothing. And somehow it is better than so many titles that I have payed for.
The game is very customizable and only requires a small amount of effort in order to mod it. I have experience in multiple coding languages so maybe I'm biased, but I found the source code very simple and user friendly. You can even create your own ships with ease! The creator encourages it and even has the game on Github for your pleasure.
The game is very casual if you want, and very intense if you want. When I started I picked a Freighter and did the merchant thing for a while. It was relaxing, carrying people and cargo back and forth for a while trying to pay off my loan, but I decided I wanted something more. So I restarted, picked an Interceptor and went out to shoot some pirates. The point is you can make the game what you want. It can be hard, easy, fast, slow, up, down, left, right, start, select, anything!
The story is very engaging! Currently there is only one storyline you can play through (The Free Worlds), but I'll be damned if that wasn't one of the best stories I have ever played. I felt connected to Freya, Katya, and Ijs, when I fought with my fleet I cared about them and each ship lost was like a knife in my heart, I had let my comrades down.
The world feels very active and busy, kind of like an Elder Scrolls game. Very rarely are things just standing around doing nothing.
I have only two problems with the game right now. The first is that sometimes there are game breaking glitches, such as when attempting to board a ship my screen would go black and I could no longer interact with anything, or when I sell the ship I'm currently piloting, but have one parked offworld and I am immediately sent to that ship.
The other problem I have is... There isn't enough! I want more! I want more Katya, I want to see Raven again, I want to learn about the Korath and the Quarg, I want to build more ships like the Dreadnought and the Kestrel, and I especially want to fight more Alphas.
This game gets a 10/10 from me and I would gladly pay money for it were it not free.

I've really enjoyed this game so if you want a bit of challenge and fancy something different with loads of character then try this game.

Your base consists of a 6 by 6 grid of land tiles, and all the tiles can be flipped in unison to reveal  6 by 6 more land tiles.  Part of the strategy is choosing when to flip your tiles during a fight.
Your base needs oxygen and adding more people requires adding more trees to compensate for oxygen usage.  In fast mode people use more oxygen than normal.  People fight melee, but if there are defense towers, then they battle first before any melee takes place.  You'll need a warehouse to collect stone, wood, chests, or fuel and then choose what other buildings (hospital, armory, artifact house, shields, trees, walls, offensive towers).  Chests are opened with keys.
Gameplay consists of flying your base from node to node through space, where nodes are either enemy bases, enemy super-bases, repair nodes, stores or treasure.  Enemy bases either wait to be attacked or attack immediately.  There are 6 enemy super-bases, and conquering them unlocks new weapons.  When all 6 super-bases are destroyed the game is won.
Pros:
- Combines game mechanics from the following genres: Tower defense, Roguelike, 4x
- Randomized maps
- Artifacts
- Early game tension
- Every enemy base you wipe out opens new weapons, which adds some variety.
Cons:
- No save.  I have beaten the game both in easy and hard modes in one sitting perhaps under an hour.  So the lack of saving is not as bad as you might think.
- The tension seems to wear off later
- There are still some bugs
- The game defaults to Russian and it's tricky to get it into English again.  It's sort of an introductory mini-game "decipher the language to find out the English setting" :)
- The game gets pretty grindy near the end.  Not being able to save is a big minus.
Is it worth $1?
No it's worth $2 or $3 - maybe even $5 after it's polished.  Get it while it's cheap and buy 3 copies to share with your friends!
Is it better than many games you pay $50?
Of course not!  Why would you think that?  Whenever you pay more money you automatically enjoy the game that much more.  Especially when titles are developed by armies of people and all of them are throwing each other under the bus and the bugs are left to the player base to catch and gripe about in the forums.  Actually this game (as far as gameplay goes) is at least as good as many higher end titles (like Civilization for example).
Is it fun?
I think so.  But buy it yourself and find out!  Get a refund if you don't like it before 2 hours are up.  I think it's well worth the time to give it a try.

Currently, this is a very stripped-down version of a FPS game. The concepts are interesting, if a bit complex, but it's not in any way finished. It's basically an early beta.
The English language setting still has Russian in it in places, and there's almost no tutorial in it at all. The graphics settings are in English, but all the other settings are in Russian. Some of the game (the early parts) are intuitive, but a lot of other parts of the game don't make any sense. Many of the written English parts are English words, but Russian syntax. There's a male and a female voice for the two genders, but both actors are obviously not fluent English speakers. The two gender models are nonconfigurable. You can't even change hair or skin color, let alone face or body shape. Forget hairstyle.
There are no real perks for grouping, even if you can figure out how to do that. You might as well solo (that's what I did). The game world is largely empty of live human players. At the same time, the community is friendly and helpful, and I didn't meet a single griefer. The game play itself is solid, little or no clipping, There are a few places where the environment interferes with movement, but it can be gotten around with only a little trouble. The difficulty starts out as essentially easy for a while, then becomes somewhat hard, and then becomes impossible. The world in many places is lethal, and you die much faster than you'd think you would, as the member of an advanced civilization. Inside the spacecraft it's safer, but the layout is confusing, and the map doesn't really show you how to get from one place to another.
Theoretically, there's going to be an update, but there's no word out on when it's coming out. There was a legal snafu with one of their programmers recently, forcing them to re-make a good chunk of their code, and this is supposedly why the long delay before the first update. I bought the game on sale, and I suggest you do the same, if you're interested in this sort of thing, can understand Russian (I can't), and/or want to support a game which may turn out to be very cool.
NOTE - MAY 17 - the game was never updated....................

First i gave this game thumb down so don't be suprised by what you are about to read in next paragraph - i will just leave here my original review for anyone to show what i thought about this game during my initial contact and how it turned out later.
[original review] Explorative linear interactive story with limited gameplay. This is the kind of game you would like to watch on youtube in no-commentary edition.
I know Bastion, it is nothing alike and i'm fine with that. In fact i was lured by the idea of futuristic turn-based skirmishes with positioning and resource-bar management. But it isn't refined and is just strictly boring.
And i am aware that this game is super-hyped and 'everyone' loves it because they have to - negative word about this game is like telling 'awww thats one ugly toddler'. You just can't say that, you have to say that it is adorable and cute.
Of course i do apreciate art style and its execution, UI, sound design, voice acting and music... but i wanted to play the game, not to have interactive slideshow with some boring, repetitive and undemanding battle sequences now and then. It is neither tactical nor arcadey...
Buy it to show devs your appreciation of their work, but do yourself a favor and just watch it on yt as somebody does all the chore while you can skip through battles and listen to another piece of story
[second impression review] So i did as i suggested in my own review - i watched this game on yt. Sudden revelation struck me that i was playing whole game wrong. I put aside keyboard and mouse and tried game pad. Much better. Controls started to make sense and game became more vivid. I didn't had to use active pause mode at all, i could issue quite precise commands in realtime. And battles werent repetitive too - game rewards you for trying new combinations of skills. Even not so useful combinations, but still you have to try it in battle if you want to uncover more of the story.
Game became more arcadey and less repetitive than i assumed. Wrong first impression turned around by diligent youtuber who showed me the way :).
Then game gets even better - you get access to the zone with special challenges where you have to either solve some 'puzzle' or fight battles using only given skills, without access to your overpowered build. This is solid. Really. First i had feeling that gameplay is average but then i tried it's full form and i had a lot of fun.
Later battles became boring, thats true. Because you will have access to all skills/functions and you will create your op-build and start pwn enemies using same combo over and over. Then you could probably say that about every game. But early, when you are still uncovering the story and completing your toolset, you will have fun with many combos and will try everything that game has to offer till you pick one combo that suits you best.
I enjoyed this game so much that i even started to want more of it. Challenge zone could have editor for user created content - new custom challenges with scoreboards, more puzzles to clear whole map during one turn in some innovative way, unlimited endless mode and so on.
Unfortunately number or challenges is really limited and you cannot access once completed challenges again.
Another issue that i have with this game is single savegame - i cannot easily start game again or have multpiple playtroughs on single account. What was the idea behind it? I can only guess.
It's curious how first impression could be so misleading so if you have concerns about this game keep in mind that i had it too, rejected this game at first and then came back to play it twice and didn't regret ;)

20 years ago in a computer far far away. . .  in 1995.  I played this game with my elder brother.  Screams of lag and KS echoed the halls.  I learned the meaning of words like camping and noob.  I rejoin it now just as I left in paused in the "entering arena" screen.  After a few more attempts to rejoin the server and voila! The game works fine.
Basically It is a simple top down shooter mmo.  Mechanics are simple shoot anyone not on your team(blue names).  Turn your ship, accelerate and decelerate, use after burners(uses energy), avoid bullets, hostile mines, long range bombs and stay alive. Be wary that firing a weapon, launching a bomb and laying a mine uses energy. ENERGY=LIFE POINTS.  IF you spam make sure you plan on not getting hit for a few seconds while you recharge.
Choose a ship, I suggest Leviathan for new guys and Warbirds when you get more experience.  Each ship has their own special abilities, some maps/game modes allow multiple abilities to be loaded at once.  Some ships can cloak, lay mines, launch long range bombs, fire bouncing bullets or even repel all hostile ordinance and ships away from you.  Again almost everything costs energy, Energy is life so spamming your gun or abilities temporarily weakens your ship and invites an easy or RNG kill form no where.  Some maps/game modes allow upgrading  max energy and energy regen they also have different objectives to win.  Despite all that variety, I'm pretty sure most people will jump into a Trench Wars map, which is the most popular and play the base modes there.
Lag is still a problem especially for those logging in far from the server.  All shots are skill based.  Learning to lead your target and hit him using the mini-map is probably the best skill to have.  That way, they only see your bullets coming in and not get a bead on your ship.  The game was worth playing and its a tiny(20 meg!) free game that will run on any hardware.

Let me put it this way:  its 20 years old, and the community is still running it all that time.  They even finally got it on Steam. This game is like Mario, its just timeless.  Yeah, its an awesome game.  Well,
an awesome game.
It's hard to review subspace because its really just a client that allows you to connect to a bunch of different gametypes all running the same engine.  Superficially, the most basic of it is that you have a keyboard controlled ship with a bunch of different actions, ranging from guns, bombs, a health pool thats also your ammo, newtonian 2D space flight mechanics, a series of useful items, warping, teleporting to teammates, script commands for the game, incredibly detailed chat interface, etc.  Every zone (server) has its own arenas (player hubs) which have their own take on the engine's settings.  All imaginable settings, textures, sounds, everything can be customized and WAS customized.  Over all of Subspace, there are thousands of arenas all with super fun gametypes, settings, textures, you name it.  The game had incredibly variety.
Not only that, the community was golden.  It was the worst and the best of the internet.  Subspace is almost timeless in that respect, as it harkens back to an era before widespread internet memes, before social media, before even places like reddit and 4_chan or major forums.  There was you, the chat, and everybody else.  It was amazing the kinds of conversations you found on this game.  Equally amazing where the efforts of people over the years as they created such intricate systems and rulesets for their zones and arenas, hosting them manually and with hardcoded administration bots.  It was a community game, run by the community by its careful, guiding hand, FOR the community.
This went on for 20 years, and slowly the game lost its population.  Zones closed down or simply lost all their players.  For a good ten years after release, the game was in its prime.  Its been in a slow, steady decline ever since then.  You can only play a game so long, ahaha.  So game was cool for a long time, even if it was decaying pretty badly towards the end.  It still had SOME charm.
That is, until getting on Steam KILLED IT.  The game is dead Jim.  You won't find any shred of its former glory.  Getting on Steam was a last ditch attempt to revive the community, get it some fresh air.  It failed so badly it depopulated one of the only remaining zones (Extreme Games).  Literally the only zone left with any playerbase at all, including stragglers, is Trench Wars.
Trench Wars used to be fantastic, as it had hundreds of arenas and minigames to play and be hosted.  Today?  Nothing is hosted anymore.  Literally the only thing that happens on Trench Wars is the public arena and javduel... javduel is entertaining for maybe a few days, that's it.
Trench Wars public arena is divided into three factions, the spec idlers (making the game a glorified chatroom instead of an actual game), the strays that don't actually play the arena's game and just fly around killing in the spawn, (aka community cancer) and the people who play the arena's game, Trench Wars basing.  Unfortunately, the basing aspect is the least populous of these three groups.
So, what has one of the greatest community run games of all time become after 20 years?  Pretty much nothing but a bunch of 1 shot Warbird ships floating around in spawn throwing potshots at each other while shouting conspiracy theories at each other.  Its... super depressing.
If you're a new guy, avoid this.  If you're a returning veteran, please turn away because you'll only be depressed by what you see after the initial waves of nostalgia wear off.

Subspace/Continuum is a top view 2D action shoot em' up game against other players. It is one of the very first Massive Multiplayer games to ever exist on the Internet. Appearing first in 1996 from Virgin Interactive, Subspace hails from an era of gaming where being able to play with and against other players was a fresh exciting concept. The game is still very active with a devoted player base that has been playing for years. Every server is called a zone, and each zone has their own unique settings and game play. Within zones exist a multitude of gameplay modes and events and leagues. Some game play modes include, Dueling, Elim, Basing and Turf warfare. Leagues are official battles between squads to determine the best squads in every zone.
Some active zones today in no particular order are; Trench Wars, Deathstarbattle, Extreme Games, Choas Zone, Hockey zone, Hyperspace, and Devastation. Trench wars is a 1 hit kill zone, Deathstarbattle requires you to wear down your opponent before making the kill and takes place inside a giant death star, currently it is the only starwars zone in existence.  EG allows for more rapid fire, and more specials in game play. Specials are ship combat accessories such as repels, thors, bricks, decoys and warps. Choas zone also has a wear them down type of game play but ships there have way more energy and everything generally does much more damage than in DSB. Hockey zone is literally what it sounds like, people can play hockey there and it's utterly awesome. Hyperspace allows you to customize and build ships, and Devastation zone, has extremely overpowered ships that provide the ultimate experience in destructive gameplay.
Subspace/Continuum is an oldie but a goldie, and definitely will provide hours of fun.

This game is so good that I am actually going to take the time to review it. Which I have never done before.
First of all, it is absolutely free. No in game charges, no pay to play, nothing. And somehow it is better than so many titles that I have payed for.
The game is very customizable and only requires a small amount of effort in order to mod it. I have experience in multiple coding languages so maybe I'm biased, but I found the source code very simple and user friendly. You can even create your own ships with ease! The creator encourages it and even has the game on Github for your pleasure.
The game is very casual if you want, and very intense if you want. When I started I picked a Freighter and did the merchant thing for a while. It was relaxing, carrying people and cargo back and forth for a while trying to pay off my loan, but I decided I wanted something more. So I restarted, picked an Interceptor and went out to shoot some pirates. The point is you can make the game what you want. It can be hard, easy, fast, slow, up, down, left, right, start, select, anything!
The story is very engaging! Currently there is only one storyline you can play through (The Free Worlds), but I'll be damned if that wasn't one of the best stories I have ever played. I felt connected to Freya, Katya, and Ijs, when I fought with my fleet I cared about them and each ship lost was like a knife in my heart, I had let my comrades down.
The world feels very active and busy, kind of like an Elder Scrolls game. Very rarely are things just standing around doing nothing.
I have only two problems with the game right now. The first is that sometimes there are game breaking glitches, such as when attempting to board a ship my screen would go black and I could no longer interact with anything, or when I sell the ship I'm currently piloting, but have one parked offworld and I am immediately sent to that ship.
The other problem I have is... There isn't enough! I want more! I want more Katya, I want to see Raven again, I want to learn about the Korath and the Quarg, I want to build more ships like the Dreadnought and the Kestrel, and I especially want to fight more Alphas.
This game gets a 10/10 from me and I would gladly pay money for it were it not free.

(This was written before EVE Online was free. I'm not stupid.)
It's like EVE Online for broke, socially awkward loners who can't pay their internet bill! (Who, me?)
-- It's free! No subscription required, needed, or existing. If you desperately want to pay money (o_O), too bad. There's no way to donate. :(
-- You can play it offline. Unless you're using the Wi-Fi at your local overpriced coffee shop to play EVE, I don't see why this would matter too much, but hey.
-- No real people, nice or otherwise. No scammers/trade hub spammers or price manipulators, but no amazing clan homies or complete strangers who give you 75 million out of the goodness of their hearts, either. You'll have to decide whether that's good or bad.
-- Gankers are still around, though. Their being NPCs doesn't change anything. Remorseless pirates with serious superiority complexes? Same as ever. If you're playing with self-imposed hard restart... I pity you. Greatly. If you weren't completely insane before you started, you probably are now.
-- No inflated prices, although some ships are pretty expensive.
-- Banks are legitimate and actually trust you enough to give you a loan. Unfortunately, it's impossible to get one big enough to make skipping out and ruining your credit score worth it.
-- There's a story, although I'm stuck at a certain point because my fleet isn't strong enough.
-- Easier ship customization and cooler builds. (Crazy fast? Can do. Extremely hard to kill? You got it. No refueling needed? Quite right. Unscannable cargo hold? Indeed, my good man.)
-- A much more casual, less intensive grind. (Endless Sky + trade route + music + relaxation = Endless Sky zen!)
-- A surprising amount of stuff to explore and discover. While you may say, "But I can look at all the ships and outfit items from the Job Board!", those are only buyable ships and items from shipyards in systems that you've visited. So unless you've explored every nook and cranny of this huge galaxy (even the apparently inaccessible bits), that's not ALL the things. Nowhere close! There are alien ships available... they're just "not available in stores".
-- It's open source.
Something you don't like or want to change? Make a plugin. Something you want to add? Go right ahead. Please. This game needs more! That is, unless you're scared of Git. No need to deny it. I don't blame you.
-- Spreadsheets optional.

Play God for once in this brilliant strategy game about contagion and extinction.
Plague Inc. Evolved sets you, a human being behind the keyboard, in the world of viral outbreaks, bacteriological contagion, and man-made epidemics set from whatever date you start playing all the way to years from now, in which your virus can either destroy or be destroyed.
The game offers various scenarios with your choice of different types of plague to choose from. Each plague has a genomic upgrade, unlocked throughout your playtime, which could make your plague superior. After that, it's all about location, location, location. Any country can start this epidemic and every country can be infected, but no country is safe.
Currently, as of Aug. 4, 2014(the date of this review), it's under construction to include a few new ways of transmitting diseases, to symptoms that could resemble everyone's favorite apocalypse, to abilities that could hinder the efforts of curing diseases, but that's not all. You will be able to create NEW SCENARIOS in the custom scenarios slot. You can mutate the common cold or make Bedbugs become the prime transmitter of your disease or redo the black plague(even though that's already a scenario in the game) which kills in a month.
Overall, the game is not complete, and with current games all for flash, bang, boom, instead of thought provoking gameplay, you won't keep entertained if you're simply a COD fan. However, if you want to play God, doom the earth to suffer the worst plague of mankind, and feel like a villain, then what are you waiting for??? YOU MOTHER, GET UP! COME ON! GET DOWN WITH THE SICKNESS!!!

This is a good start to a game. I believe all the haters claiming that this is just ripping off minecraft just don't understand this project. Now that's not to say this isn't "inspired" by minecraft, but there are plenty of games of that type.
The creator(s) say "I want to involve the community in very early stages of this game.",  "I´m hoping to get feedback from players who are helping to shape the game's destiny, and excited to get access to the game before it's fully released." and "Adding user created content is the primary target of the Voxelized. I highly trust to the Steam community that they all will help me to develop a game that has those features which they want"
This game may be another cube based voxel, but its not about what the game is. It's about what we, the community, and the creators make it.

After the succes of Minecraft, many voxel based games have seen the light here on Steam. Some are pretty good, some are pretty bad. Some are shooter based, some RPG based and others are survival based. Voxelized, on the other hand, casts all these things aside and focuses solely on the building part, which obviously was one of the main reasons why Minecraft became so popular.
Aside from walking around there are two things you can do in Voxelized (at the moment): remove blocks (leftmouse) and add blocks (rightmouse). In the time I was playing I was not able to add blocks, so I tried to check the controls in the option menu to see if I was doing something wrong. Apparently, you can not change the controls in the menu, in fact it even says "Still Under Construction". In my opinion, Early Access or not, something like a game menu should work.
Right now, Voxelized has rain and snow, which is nice but the game only comes with just a different blocks/textures, so you will probably get bored with it quickly.
Being in Early Access, Voxelized might still improve and the developer seems to listen to the players but even if the developer adds all these things like; animals, weapons and multiplayer support, you just get another Minecraft.
