So to start this off, I think it's worth mentioning my somewhat lacking MMO experience. When in like 5th grade, I played Runescape (mostly because I didn't know there were more MMOs), a couple years after that I played a lot of Maplestory, then after that I played a lot of League of Legends (if that counts at all), then I bounced between a lot of MMOs looking for that experience everyone else was getting into with stuff like WoW (which I didn't have the money for at the time). I really wanted to find something good, but there was always some...level of jankyness about other MMOs I've tried. They felt weird, the inventory management and stuff was always clunky, the worlds were largely uninteresting, and the games were largely unhelpful in terms of actually finding the content worth finding. They felt unpolished, and I couldn't get into them.
From the very first moments for playing Final Fantasy XIV, I knew I was going to love it. Everything
good. The world was interesting, there was actually a
. The game looks really good and feels like a Final Fantasy game, a series I've loved since I was a kid pretending that I knew how to play Final Fantasy 7 and 8 on my brother's PS1. It has a lot of helpful resources in game to help you learn things, and the community is incredibly helpful, too. I can number my bad experiences with other players on one hand.
Despite being what is described as a "tab-target" MMO, the combat feels good. Every class seems to be worth playing and they all have their merits and feel good. Animations on spells and attacks feel pretty good and it has a nice quick pace to it. If combat isn't quite your speed, crafting is totally worth diving into. It has a lot of cool risk and reward going on with the crafting system, and it's a great way to make gil and great equipment. Usually I think of crafting as an afterthought, but in FFXIV I feel like it's a significant part of the game and the community.
An added bonus is that playing this game on a controller is totally viable and is also my preferred method of playing, I think it feels way better to move with a stick and have my shortcuts all in one place instead of having to stretch my hand across my keyboard. Using a Steam Controller on this game has its merits as well, with easier mouse control and being able to set some neat little shortcuts to help things go a bit smoother.
My few problems with the game are mostly technical issues. The DX11 version of the game has issues that I (as well as others) have experienced and have thus needed to switched to the DX9 version which has decent performance and a slight graphical downgrade. Registering for this through steam and making an account was pretty weird, too.
Also playing a gathering class is boring as hell, even if it's a good way to make money and get those all-important materials for crafting.
I give it a...
The Sub Was Worth It/10
Added: Something seriously worth mentioning is that the expansion rarely goes on sale on Steam. I would highly recommend getting this game from somewhere else because it is frequently on sale or just flat out cheaper. Although if you made an account and did the free trial through steam you will need to purchase the steam version of the game to continue with that character.

Ndemic Creations created Plague Inc: Evolved, a game so brilliant that once you start playing it, you become so involved that when the cure starts being produced, you start to worry.
Plague Inc: Evolved is the second game by Ndemic creations, the first being Plague Inc. It features you as a controller of a disease, what type of disease? Any type that you want. There are many different plagues to pick from and there are even official scenarios like the Black Plague, or global warming. So many different ways to start your game. And that's the best way to start a game.
You pick a name, special genes you unlock by infecting the world that can help you play a starting country and Patient Zero has been released. The game is a little bit slow at the beginning but once you have the points to pick symptoms and ways to infect other people, the game becomes quite fast paced and you have to click on many things. Bubbles appear everywhere, the levels of infected people rises, and before you know it you have infected the world and started to kill (or enslave) them.
The game has beautiful detail, everything you need to see is 3D modelled, for example, the planes and boats you see going around infecting countries are 3D, they have depth, even though usually people play on top speed so you don't even see them for long enough. It's this kind of small details that makes a game great, the creators finding all the issues and designing every aspect, even if it isn't all that necessary.
There are so many different ways to infect the world, you can go straight in with coughs, sneezes and cysts and get noticed quickly, or you can be stealthy and infect everyone with no symptoms and then order the plague to kill, not just that but with plagues like Bio-weapon, the plague starts killing almost instantly, so you get noticed quickly and need to adapt your disease to infect faster than people are dying. Another example of different ways to win is the Necroa Virus, also known as the Zombie Virus, yes this game has a plague that lets you command zombies, make them aggressive or send them to distant lands to infect the country, you decide. A final example of this is the Neurax Worm, it’s a parasite that attaches itself to the human brain, and when you decide it to, controls the brain to do what you want. Whether that’s to go on a plane to a target country, find earthworms, commit suicide or even treat your Neurax Worm like a god and worship it. It's yours to control.
The game is currently being updated at a relatively slow pace but with good reason. They are making the updates fair sized instead of tiny updates that add one thing. They are translating the game into other languages, working to add custom scenarios and even let people infect the world side by side with another player.
Definitely the game to own if you like plagues and viruses, or if you like controlling an extremely realistic disease. Definitely worth every cent I paid for it. With many different ways to win Plague Inc: Evolved, this is a game of coughs, sneezes and choices.
I rate this game 10/10, a game you don’t even need a brain slug to tell you it’s great.

Note: While the review may suggest this, I do not hate this game - especially considerig the developer has the sensability to have a "choose how much you pay" option ranging from free to a modest 4.99. That said, I'm going to be reviewing from the perspective of how much I liked or disliked the game.

Tl;dr at the bottom
Maybe it doesn't help I didn't give this game more than a few minutes of a chance, but I can't say that I really "liked" it. Granted when it comes to CYOA fiction, that I like the more fantastic end of the spectrum in terms of story and writing, but even judging the story from the writing contained within itself, I would have to say I did not like it.
Don't get me wrong, the story here is relatable and sound in itself, but I did not feel the impact of it as a choose your own adventure game with "branching naratives" as it went on. In fact, I felt like I was being pulled along a predestined path the entire way through to the point I might have appreciated this more if it were more along the lines of a visual novel than a choose your own adventure. Why? Because while visual novels are essentially visual choose your own adventures, VNs have a little more of an exceptance within it's community for stories that go one particular way, considering there's something to look at besides the text often. Here, I feel as though the text alone is not enough to sell the game for me.
In a way, I felt the illusion of choice was strong here, as though no matter what I chose, I would end up in the same place every time - and a little betrayed when I recalled all the little telltale esque "Emily will remember this" things at the bottom of the chat box. In a way, I would compare this game more to mad-libs than anything else. Which is fine, but keep in mind that this is still supposed to be a game. Not something where you just fill in the blanks with pre-determined choices that don't impact the way the story branches away from different endings.
This game would have benefited from two things: one, a wider branched narative and some larger degree of interactivity which the player could interact with on the screen - like learning about things within the narative via interactions on the desktop. The reason I say this is because I never felt like I was playing as "me" in the game, but rather that I was being pushed to play as a "nice guy" who was supposed to tell Emily that her boyfriend was terrible or inadiquette and that she deserved better.
In fact, I feel that's the thing that bothers me about the game was that it played just like I were a person who just assumed her boyfriend or anyone she liked - anyone that was not Emily - was terrible. I noted several times I would read about characters who I never even met, or rather never recieved any context about, I would just automatically have the option to call them a♥♥♥♥♥♥ I don't know if those styles of choice would gave resulted in a similar manner to the very last sequence in the game, in which typing leads to deletion of what you meant to say (something that was downright frustrating considering the game was actively taking choice away from me), but it still felt out of place without necessary context.
Not to mention Emily herself, I have no idea how to feel about that because I have had such little interaction with her as a player. I know nothing about her besides her being a college student with varying degrees of angst. She may not be a bad character or a bad person overall. In fact I feel it's the author's fault for not handing more context to who she was and why we as the player character should care about her. There's no notes, no conversations, no nothing that discusses who Emily is, why you should care about her, or why you should care about the fact that she has a boyfriend who (as far as you know) only has lightweight arguments with her.
I refuse to give this game the leighway of being "art" and that's why I don't understand why it's story is so much left without context, because the fact remains that there was control given to the player, and they were expected to make decisions AS that character - but without any information those decisions come across as uneducated, the superficial results come across as unfair during the first playthrough, and it ultimately ends as an experiance that left more to be desired.
That said, I do hope to see more from the developer - better work preferably. Something with more interactivity, something where choices matter, and something that's designed to do more than make a statement which is up to the player's interpretation.
Tl;dr
-The story is sound, but subpar due to the lack of context and ability to make your own choices
-The characters, including the Player Character which is supposed to be you come across as assuming at best, and annoying at worst.
-Limited interactivity, which is a shame for a game boasting to have a "branching narative" that takes place on a desktop and all you can access are the IM pages which don't have much interesting elements to it.
Overall, this game could be way better. But as I said, it's worth trying because it's free and it's short. So if you feel as though you wasted your time as I did, you're only wasting a half an hour of time you probably weren't spending doing anything better.

Knowing nothing about the game except that the screenshots reminded me of the "Escape Velocity" series, I decided to give it a try. I didn't then, and still don't know if the similarities between the two games are intentional or not, but they are absolutely there. I have only played the game for a couple of hours so far, but it still feels like it is nearly the same game.
If you've never played any of the Escape Velocity games, I would go so far as to say that you missed out big time on those. There is good news though! This free game is a way to (kind of) rectify this!
Now, obviously I am biased because the game reminds me so much of another title that I enjoyed. However, there's a lot of reason to like the game because of that. You start off in a sandbox universe that you can pretty much do what you want in. Do you want to earn your keep by transporting passengers around? You can do that. Perhaps you want to trade goods and earn your money through piloting a freighter. Well, you can do that too. Do those sound too similar? Well, then perhaps you should go hunt pirates instead. Don't want to hunt pirates? Then maybe you should BE a pirate. You can do that too.
I haven't gotten far enough into the game to really comment on the story, but if it occurs the same way it did in Escape Velocity, it will happen over the course of your gameplay, and will tailor itself to you based on what you are doing. That means of course, that seeing where the story can take you will require experimenting with different playstyles. Now obviously this is just a guess, but the rest of the game is similar enough that I would be surprised if the story elements didn't function the same way.
I would say that, as a gamer, you are doing yourself a disservice by not trying this game. Especially considering it does not cost you anything but time to do so. A lot of people comment on the game being free, and you will see why everyone seems so surprised this does not cost anything once you load it up yourself.

Before saying any other thing:
I tend to only buy games with a discount in Steam, and I can say that this game is worth every cent.
For being an Early Access title, since the first version I played feel like a complete game. If you are interested in sinking several hours in a single game, this is your game. If you want to learn or practice programming skills, this is your game. If you want a game with a sense of progression, this is your game. If you have OCD, it’ll take you a good time putting all in its place.
But, if you´re interested in other things like stunning graphics, easy mechanics or a game that does not require you to learn lots of things or lots of work to do, you should consider this one.
Also, a couple of things to consider: The objective is there, but there’s no history or anything like that. There is a tutorial, but (at least for me) doesn’t feel very clear and I have to say that it requires previous knowledge of mechanisms and logic gates to get it working properly. Also the music doesn’t even feel like is there, so better to prepare a custom playlist before start playing it.
Moreover, the community at least in my opinion, is very good and the developers put a lot of work in this game, at the point of giving us every Friday an update on what is being added to the game or the new features, mechanics, parts or textures. And if you are someone who thinks that games are only for the young people, for entertainment or just to dump hours in a useless task with no benefits, I swear this game can change your opinion about gaming.
And before anyone points out my hours on record, maybe I have to say I only open it 4 times and I am aware that I haven’t put the time this game deserves, but I got an automatic factory working, probably because I have experience in micromanaging, and mechanisms.
Antes de decir cualquier otra cosa:
Yo suelo sólo comprar juegos cuando están en descuento en Steam, y puedo decir que este juego vale cada centavo.
Para ser un juego de acceso anticipado, desde la primera versión que jugué me pareció un juego completo. Si lo que buscas es pasar varias horas en un solo juego, busca aquí. Si estas aprendiendo o quieres practicar programación, busca aquí. Si quieres algo con sentido de progresión, busca aquí. Si tienes TOC, pasaras un buen rato organizando cosas.
Pero si tus intereses son cosas como gráficos destacables, mecánicas fáciles o un juego que no necesite que aprendas mucho o pongas bastante trabajo en él, mejor considera buscar en otro lado.
Tiene algunos detalles a tomar en cuenta: hay un objetivo principal pero no una historia que lo aborde. Si eres alguien que piensa que los juegos son sólo para jóvenes, para entretenerse o para desperdiciar horas en una tarea inútil, este juego puede cambiar tu punto de vista inclusive sobre toda la industria de los videojuegos.
Antes de que alguien mencione las horas de juego que tengo, quizá debería aclarar que lo he abierto unas 4 veces y estoy consciente de que no he dado el tiempo que este juego merece, no obstante logre hacer una fábrica automática, probablemente porque ya tenía algo de experiencia en microcontrol y mecanismos.

At the time of writing this, I bought this game about 24 hours ago. At the time of writing this, I also have a little over 13 hours into this game(Despite having beaten it before buying it on Steam). That alone tells you how awesome this game is, Everything from it's incredible and exciting storyline to the street vendors' dialogue is as close to perfect as I've seen.
Pros:
- The main storyline (All Sun On Yee-related missions) is like being in a really good action movie. That's the best way I can describe it. The writing, cinematography, and character development is spot-on.
- The characters is this game feel like real people. The writing and voice acting is superb. This, both fortunately and unfortunately makes it easy to get connecting to a character. You'll understand why that's a "bad" things when you play.
- The environment of Hong Kong iss so many different great things. It's gritty, dirty, vibrant, bright, dark, beautiful, etc. It's what it needs to be when that is appropriate. You never feel out of place in this game unless the game wants you to feel out of place. Also, civilian dialogue in this game is great. It acts as a comic-relief and is probably my favorite thing about this game, other than the pork buns.
- The combat in this game, both melee and armed, is great. Abviously it has a much more in-depth melee system, but the gunplay is fun and satisfying as well. I've always thought of the melee in this game as what The Batman: Arkham wanted to be. It's fluid, fun. and cool looking, but it's also challenging and requires more than button-mashing most of the time. You're also able to use several objectsin the environment like phone boothes, ovens, and hook to kill and dismember your opponents, which is just awesome.
Cons:
-This game is pretty glitchy. Not mentioning the first port of this game on PC, which literally didn't work, this game has a lot of things that look a little off. It's always something small like a floating cell phone or someone running in circles. Every once in a while you'll car will launch its self a little ways or Wei will get thrown into the air by the terrain, but I neer encountered anything that took me out of the experience.
- I wore a cop outfit this entire playthrough and, while hilarious, it's a little odd that you can do that. There were many laughs to be had when I was doing gang-activities in full police gear.Just a small thing, though. It's the outfit I chose to wear so you don't have to.
Sleeping Dogs is, for lack of a better word, fun, which is truly the most important thing any video game could ever be. It may just be a niche thing for me but it's everything I want in a video game. It's deep without taking itself too seriously. It's funny without resorting to gross-out humor or♥♥♥♥♥♥jokes. The pacing makes it fun and fair through the whole game. And most of all, the tutorials in this game aren't just boxes telling you what buttons to press. You learn through the game, which is a mark of a great game to me.

I've played this game for a very long time (before hooking it up to my Steam account). If you're looking for a hunting game, here's a summary and the pros and cons.
Summary:
The game is a hunting simulator with a lot of variety in terms of animals, maps/environments, and weapons. It has a skill system to let your time invested actually show progress (tracking, shooting, etc), and aims for a good balance of realism and fun, tending strongly toward realism. You WILL have to spend an hour or more to find a high-scoring animal in many cases, but the animal population is far more dense and high-scoring than in real life. It isn't a shooter where animals will run all over and be easy targets, it's a game of patience for reward, and using common sense, skill and experience to track and kill your targets.
Pros:
- Free to play, with free animal rotation (several animals are always free to hunt, others require licenses unless on weekly free rotation)
- Not pay-to-win--while some purchasable items give advantages, they aren't necessary at all (except in unusual cases of the free rotation animals needing a different legal ammunition than you can get with the free basic shotgun + rifle--not sure that can happen)
- Realistic, relatively immersive, and very beautiful landscapes
- A wide range of environments (American swamp/woodland/meadow, European forest/alpine mountains, Australian outback, Alaskan winter coast, etc) with a large number of huntable species
- Fairly realistic overall animal behavior, and some very nice models
- Some animals have coat variations, including normal variations, very rare non-typical antlers, and even rarer color mutations (piebald, albino, melanistic, leucistic)
- Seasonal and holiday events offering small but fun rewards
- Constant competitions that award $em (the in-game currency purchased with real money) for placing 1st-3rd, and trophies
- A skill-up system that benefits you by providing more, and more accurate, information on tracks the more you track (species-specific skills), and gives you a steadier aim with weapons as you grow more proficient with each
- A second type of currency ($gm) awarded through comprehensive in-game missions that allows you to buy most consumeables: ammunition (the basic weapons have unlimited free ammo), scent sprays, dog treats, etc
- A fairly close-knit community, if you like that sort of thing, on the forum--with very fast customer service responses should you need them. As an example, one member posted his process of designing a recurve bow in real life, and the design team put it into the game to honor it.
Cons:
- Most of the camouflages, weapons, animal callers/lures, stands, blinds and licenses cost real money (via $em purchases), not the mission-awarded money, to purchase--while available in sales bundles, buying a significant amount of items can add up very quickly. You do not NEED to buy these items, but for example hunting elk without an elk caller can be very difficult. You CAN buy scents for $gm instead, but they have 50 uses.
- To be able to hunt all animals at all times, rather than relying on the free rotation, you will need to buy a membership (not really a con; they are very very cheap, but it's notable for those unaware). You can buy individual timed licenses for $gm, but they are very comparatively "expensive." (It's really worth it to get the 3-month basic membership, it's just a few dollars)
- Some animals do have wonky animations, nothing too serious; likewise there's always a few floating rocks and trees in the very large maps, but devs are consistently fixing what is reported
- The loading range could be better--animals will "blink" out of existence at about 400-450 yards, I forget which, until you get closer again--my biggest gripe
- Very little animal interaction--while they move in realistic group types (i.e. bachelor herds, mixed groups or solo) depending on species, no animals currently fight, and the only predator/prey interaction is wolves occasionally chasing elk. It can be a little disconcerting to see a bear standing next to a deer!
All in all I think it is by far the best hunting game out there, easy to get lost in its zen space as you wander the very detailed, beautiful landscapes. The game's players include a large number of actual hunters, so I figure it's probably fairly close to the real thing, enough to be entertaining. The psychology of the luck of the draw--whether that deer you're tracking/calling in is going to be a little buck or a monster trophy--can be both addicting and rewarding, and it's easy to put the game down and come back a week or two later and still have plenty of fun.
TL;DR, Best hunting game currently on the market (imo), worth the download if you're wanting to try one, good community/dev team and beautiful game to lose yourself in at a relaxing pace with occasional thrills. Best played with around $20 input for a membership (unlimited basic free ammo + licenses) and a caller or two, but playable without.

As I mention in the video below, I've been playing Beat 'Em Ups since elementary school.  They've always been one of my favorite genres of games.  From Bad Dudes and River City Ransom to Final Fight and Streets of Rage, I've played them all.
Mother Russia Bleeds is a more than welcome addition to the Beat 'Em Up family.  The pixel art is excellent, the story is generic (that's a good thing), the main characters all have strengths and weaknesses to fit your specific style of play, and (and this is the most important part) it's explicitly violent.
Tips:
- Go ahead and do the tutorial.  It'll get you used to the controls.  Not all Beat 'Em Ups are created equal.
- USE THAT DASH.  Defeating many of the bad guys depends on your dashing out of their way.  Some will give tells to let you know they're about to dash towards YOU.  You can also hold Dash button (R1) and either Punch (X) or Kick (Y) to do a dashing attach.  This will save your butt in many situations, but especially when there are too many enemies on the screen and you need to break away.
- Manage Your Health and Nekro.  I kept forgetting that my health bar and Nekro syringe were both in the upper right hand corner and to keep and eye out on them, so I died a lot more than I wanted to.  Clear the area, watch for twitching victims, and extract Nekro from them while you can.  You can even Dash Attack out to attack enemies sneaking up behind you, then go back and get more.
10/10.  Would punch the s*it out of a full sized adult pig again.

Solo: 7/10 Multi: 8/10
4 things that shined:
-The beat'em up was a nice mix of nostalgia with gore. The combat is only slightly more complex than beat'em ups from the SNES era, but the small additions go a very long way. (IE Grabbing dudes in a beat'em up is common, but grabbing them, having a directional throw, and tons of combo/coop potential from there is uncommon)
-The soundtrack is pretty cool, very fitting to everything happening. Trippy and haunting :)
-Great style. Think: If the guys who did Hotline Miami reskinned TMNT.
-The Dodge button is clutch, I had to go back and edit this review and the score even, just because the dodge button is both so responsive and well-integrated. Well-integrated meaning the dash button will effectively make all other buttons a new button, even jump has a different trajectory.
3 things that were found flaccid:
-Pretty much everything you can do wrong in a boss battle is done wrong here. -Everything- Too gimmicky, too hard at times, too easy at others, dense with mobs because alone the boss is underwhelming
-You will get rag-dolled constantly. If you thought Ivan being on super-soldier steroids would stop a dog that is 200 pounds lighter than him from throwing him to the ground like a shriveled corpse, you are sadly mistaken. Many insignificant
-The difficulty spikes range from a gentle breeze on the hardest difficulty, and wondering who was experiencing bath salt induced hatred for certain part when on the easiest setting.
I recommend this, definitely better with people, but as a single player experience:
7/10
With friends: (Was tempted to go higher, but when you're 'altered' with good friends every game is a 10)
8/10

Okay, totally overhauled review.
The Beat 'em Up is my favourite genre of game of all time. I play Streets of Rage 2 at least once every month or so. My love for this genre goes deep, Aliens Vs Predator, Battle Circuit, Ninja Baseball Batmen, Double Dragon Advance, God Hand are among many examples of the genre that I absolutely love. So I was pretty psyched when Mother Russia Bleeds got announced.

For the first day the controls were totally borked as most USB controllers wouldn't work but that's been fixed, yay!
So...oh god, so I've sunk like 5 hours into the arena mode...and okay, so the fighting systems is pretty fun if a bit simple, you have a light attack that can be charged up and heavy attack that can be chained with the light attacks and pretty light grappling/takedown system (some reverse grapples, supers and specails woulda been nice but whatevs) also it has guns in it sometimes which really bugs me because in a Beat 'em Up I want punch mooks not shoot dudes. It's important.
I like the art style a lot but it's hard to take seriously with how very hard it tries to be edgy all of the time but the music is pretty consistently awesome for the most part and helps nail down the tone of the game.
It's also a game featuring homophobic/transphobic garbage but at least you can be a girl I suppose? Also you beat junkies and dogs to death, yay.
It's dumb as a brick covered in puke...even so...I kinda still like...somehow? It's like if Hobo with a Shotgun was a a Beat 'Em Up except without a shred of self-awareness. The game is just a big filth wallow.
So, If you like Beat 'Em Ups and have a strong stomach then Mother Russia Bleeds is worth try for sure but it's really just okay.
If you wanna play a really solid Beat 'Em Up on the Steams that does new and different things, has great pixel graphics and a bit of actual depth I'd honestly recommend trying Devils Dare instead.

Jeremiah DeWitt receives a letter from an old schoolmate. However, this cryptic message prompts him to go to his friend's manor as he's aware that something had gone wrong. This is his first step towards madness, horror, darkness...
The Last Door is an episodic game, with four chapters. All of them is following DeWitt's fate and search for the truth. But while you're witnessing his adventure, cutscenes show also a doctor being worried for DeWitt and began to search for him. The plot is full of mystery, the more you're going forward, the less you can grasp the reality of the whole story. Well, it's still very foggy for me though I may have a general idea of what's happening. No wonder that there is a second season where you're the doctor...
The Letter is the beginning of DeWitt's adventure. He's investigating his friend's manor. Everything seems normal but when you know where to look, it seems that this manor has seen a tragedy...
DeWitt, after finding his friend's body, comes back to his boarding school, now an hospice. Searching for clues to explain what's happening to his schoolmates, he begins to remember what they have done back then...
After being knocked down by his ancient teacher's servant and after discovering the horrifying truth, DeWitt finds himself in one of these creepy neighboorhoods of London. A man seems to appear and to disappear, like he was inviting DeWitt to follow him...
DeWitt found himself in a remote manor, where one of his classmates are residing. However, while investigating it, everything seems to suggest that Alexandre has gone far into his research...
As you can see, the more you're advancing in the story, the more horror you'll discover. Besides, be prepare yourself to some scares (I got one) and to people that aren't real (or are they just a fragment of DeWitt's imagination?).
The Last Door is a great example of how a plot must be delivered. Not too revealing at the beginning and then only, plant some clues and hints that will put a seed of doubt in your mind, until you're arriving at the end without too much clarity but with a general idea of what's happening.
The gameplay is a point-and-click: you have items to examine, to take, to combine and to use. You have also some puzzles, though they're a rarity in the game. Your inventory is in the bottom of your screen, making it easier for you to use objects. It's staying in place, never going down. You speak also with people: you can choose your lines, however, while some can be always asked, other ones are very important. And when you have a new piece of information, you can question again people.
You have also notes to read in all chapters, which will give you some clues on what's going on. Also, you can hunt some paranormal or strange actions, however, they're often secrets requiring to be fast or to avoid to do something or to just stay for a few minutes where you are.
However, be prepared also to some slow passages. Indeed, when DeWitt is holding a lantern, you're walking slowy, without any fast footstep.  There is also a passage where he's kinda out of it, so, be patient.
The graphics are belonging to the retro era. I mean by that it's pixelised like a good old adventure game. You can't see any of the reactions of the characters, however, every area of interest are shown thanks to a magnifying glass with a yellow border.
The soundtrack is also captivating. It's really fitting to the story and to the atmosphere. I really like the opening.
The Last Door is really a masterpiece for the price. It's one of the best little adventure games that I've played. Everything is nearing perfection or is perfect. Go for it!

I vaguely remember encountering a prologue to a title named
in Kongregate a couple years ago, but I dropped participating Kongregate community sometime thereon, so it was a complete surprise encountering the full game here in Steam later. A quick research informed me about the Kickstarter journey of The Game Kitchen and how wonderful a job they managed to put on the table with limited participation on backers and pixel art graphics only. Recently completing the first season, here will be my part actual review and part fangirl rant for Victorian Gothic - especially for the concept of horror itself.
It's 1891, England. Jeremiah Devitt receives an unsettling letter from his old friend, Anthony Beechworth, with whom he attended a boarding school in Aberdeen years ago. The letter contains one sentence only that would be vaguely familiar to Devitt: "Videte ne quis sciat", the long forgotten motto of the philosophy club they formed as young boys back in the boarding school. Knowing his old friend would only use this sentence as a distress call, Devitt leaves his apartment and catches the first train to Sussex to visit Beechworth residence. From thereon, his journey towards the unknown, the unspeakable and the unforeseeable will begin. In his journey for discovering the truth, Devitt will slowly yet surely pass the veil that separates the wisdom from the insanity, reaching for the knowledge of "Malum in se" or rather: evil within itself.
As one can get a grasp of the narration so far,
is a fine product of horror literature, inspired heavily from the works of Poe, Lovecraft, Maupassant, Borges, Machen and many others; playing on the horror of the unknown, the unexplainable or more so: the uncanny. Today, literary academics make clear differentiations between the notions of fear, terror and the horror. Fear is an instantaneous reaction or at least a basic worry, while the terror is being continuously under some kind of threat. With terror, you can fundamentally foresee and understand the threat that would befall on you, yet fail to resolve it or prevent it with a conclusion. With horror, on the other hand, you are rendered incapable of even grasping the meaning, the reason or the nature of the threat altogether, rendering your cognitive ability useless… and that specific kind of threat is the most fundamental, basic and dreadful experience anyone can go under. So dreadful, the narrative medium of language fails to describe its nature exactly, presenting only vague descriptions of associations. Being a masterfully arranged horror adventure,
is one of such experiences.
Establishing a horror adventure with pixel art graphics might seem like a repelling choice for most people, but I find part game's success in this specific display choice. With pixel art graphics, we are not always capable of understanding direct depictions of objects, nuances or happenstances. We are left with symbolic environment designs that are presented to arrange a vague image, a symbol for the actual. It is both familiar yet quite so alien at the same time. Freud's 1835 Article,
or
describes this specific notion as a cognitive dissonance; for being attracted and repulsed by a concept at the same time. This paradoxical nature deems a state or a being uncanny - and quite possibly dangerous. This fundamental concept perpetuated the fear of the unknown and established the foundation of all horror literature that will follow involuntarily. The art display in the game is an excellent example of Freud's Uncanny. Everything is somewhat familiar yet boundlessly alien at the same time. This psychodynamic arranges a triumphant baseline for the atmosphere. The same notion is supported by brilliantly picked sound effects and orchestrated soundtrack – ordinary and beautiful, yet unexplainable and unsettling at the same time - to exalt the setting.
Aside its psychological undertone,
is an episodic point & click adventure. Each chapter follows the one before to portray the first season of Jeremiah Devitt's unsettling journey. You are to roam within a limited environment in each chapter; collecting notes, items; interacting with people and solving puzzles to make the story progress. Even with the chosen style of graphics, it’s not that hard to notice and interact with objects. Puzzles take brief contemplation at first, but when figured, they are spot on and elegant. Anecdotes and nuances collected from the most memorable Gothic literary pieces are masterfully nestled into the game for your discovery. The primary motifs of the game - crows, or rather ravens - are a direct reference to Poe alongside countless others.
If you are interested in the collective experience that would portray the totality of
, you are in for a literary feast with imageries worthy of nightmarish depictions scribbled into your subconscious. It is a remarkable example of sheer success for both narrative and atmosphere without much graphic display. Recommended to be played with headphones and in total darkness!

Ndemic Creations created Plague Inc: Evolved, a game so brilliant that once you start playing it, you become so involved that when the cure starts being produced, you start to worry.
Plague Inc: Evolved is the second game by Ndemic creations, the first being Plague Inc. It features you as a controller of a disease, what type of disease? Any type that you want. There are many different plagues to pick from and there are even official scenarios like the Black Plague, or global warming. So many different ways to start your game. And that's the best way to start a game.
You pick a name, special genes you unlock by infecting the world that can help you play a starting country and Patient Zero has been released. The game is a little bit slow at the beginning but once you have the points to pick symptoms and ways to infect other people, the game becomes quite fast paced and you have to click on many things. Bubbles appear everywhere, the levels of infected people rises, and before you know it you have infected the world and started to kill (or enslave) them.
The game has beautiful detail, everything you need to see is 3D modelled, for example, the planes and boats you see going around infecting countries are 3D, they have depth, even though usually people play on top speed so you don't even see them for long enough. It's this kind of small details that makes a game great, the creators finding all the issues and designing every aspect, even if it isn't all that necessary.
There are so many different ways to infect the world, you can go straight in with coughs, sneezes and cysts and get noticed quickly, or you can be stealthy and infect everyone with no symptoms and then order the plague to kill, not just that but with plagues like Bio-weapon, the plague starts killing almost instantly, so you get noticed quickly and need to adapt your disease to infect faster than people are dying. Another example of different ways to win is the Necroa Virus, also known as the Zombie Virus, yes this game has a plague that lets you command zombies, make them aggressive or send them to distant lands to infect the country, you decide. A final example of this is the Neurax Worm, it’s a parasite that attaches itself to the human brain, and when you decide it to, controls the brain to do what you want. Whether that’s to go on a plane to a target country, find earthworms, commit suicide or even treat your Neurax Worm like a god and worship it. It's yours to control.
The game is currently being updated at a relatively slow pace but with good reason. They are making the updates fair sized instead of tiny updates that add one thing. They are translating the game into other languages, working to add custom scenarios and even let people infect the world side by side with another player.
Definitely the game to own if you like plagues and viruses, or if you like controlling an extremely realistic disease. Definitely worth every cent I paid for it. With many different ways to win Plague Inc: Evolved, this is a game of coughs, sneezes and choices.
I rate this game 10/10, a game you don’t even need a brain slug to tell you it’s great.

I would like to see some additional special features to different diseases, such as the nanovirus being able to hack into power plants, military etc. Maybe add some more special symptoms, like have the fungus engage in mind control causing people to jump off of high ledges to spread the spores within the body.
I definitely do enjoy this game, it is very fun to try to destroy the world. Just wanted to give some posssible alternative options.

looks and plays like a hidden-object game, with all of the actual HO scenes removed.  It has the usual melodramatic story with all the favourite elements of HOG storylines (female protagonist faces supernatural evil, rescues loved one, redeems villain.) In exchange for the lost HO games, even more running about of various plot coupons is involved.  Most of the gameplay, really, revolves around trying to remember where you saw some kind of lock, now that you've found the object that serves as the key.
Graphics and sound are decent, though nothing extraordinary. The puzzles typical of an HO game are here, too.  They're not very hard, but they're done well enough.  In fact, I might grudgingly recommend this game for people who love the flavour of HO games, but hate actually hunting hidden objects, if it weren't for one problem; the game is glitchy.  The discussion forum has plenty of threads from people who encountered game-breaking glitches.  For my own part, I got a glitch-free run up to the final cutscene, where the game crashed completely.  Thereafter, I could never play it again, because it would crash immediately upon loading -- even after an uninstall/reinstall.
The combination of the limited gameplay and the game's apparent determination to commit suicide seals my verdict on this one;  look elsewhere for your next HO gaming fix.

Despite its shortness and myriads of half-empty scenes, Cursed is a fun casual adventure game (not a HOG though). But, by the gods, the voice acting is more wooden than the Amazonian rainforest.
Probably the best way to describe Cursed is that it is a monster hunting point ‘n’ click adventure game, which is so casual that its challenge level practically drifts into nothingness.
Despite not being a hidden object game, Cursed carries quite a few elements associated with that genre. This includes the plot itself: a worried bride is looking for her missing fiancé, who is held captive in a mansion filled with Universal movie monsters. So, she does the natural thing of finding weapons to murder each of these monsters until she reaches the end credits. And I would swear that one of those weapons is her voice acting.
Gameplay is so easy that Cursed could almost be viable as an education game on casual adventures. It has a large gameplay area but only a handful of actual tasks, so most of the time is spent travelling. Even with this, it barely lasts two hours at most, but at least those are two very laid-back, fun little hours.

is an isometric strategy adventure game starring Red, a voiceless entertainer and her anonymous lover, the latter trapped inside a sword-shaped tool known as the Transistor. Join Red and her mentor-turned-weapon through an epic adventure that explores the concept of singularity and discover the secrets of the city of Cloudbank and the mysterious Camerata family.
manages to take some interesting ideas and delivers them in an interesting way. Though there are a few cutscenes, most of the story is disclosed through the brief (but frequent), private whispers of the Transistor. Red happily listens, creating an authentic, naturally-developing emotional foundation between Red and her weapon.
The story arc is a little predictable and some events could have been presented in more straightforward manners.
has interesting characters and lore but a fair amount of it requires some critical thinking, assumption and the reading of hidden message terminals that share additional information about the city of Cloudbank and a mysterious event known as "The Process".
The story is overall pleasant, in large part due to the dramatic monologues of the man inside the Transistor. The game can be completed within 6 hours.
A mix of fast-paced action and turned-based strategy best describes the game's mechanics. You'll explore a large (though linear) world and frequently encounter mobs of enemies. Using dozens of unlockable Functions, you can tailor your own combat builds in very specific ways for unique effects and take them to battle.
's combat can be played in live action at full-speed or can be played in a turn-based manner by stopping time and planning attack sequences in advance. The latter is advantageous, as it allows you to use multiple moves in much quicker succession than is possible in full-speed action.
You'll be spending quite some time learning the different Functions and the different enemies and how they react to each other. When you're not fighting, you're exploring a distopian virtual city while listening to the melancholy of the man inside the Transistor.
Oh! One button is specially assigned to a singing mechanic; holding it makes Red hum to the tune of the music at any given time. Fun touch.
You know that feeling when you look at concept art for a game and think "Wow, this looks amazing!" and then the game itself looks somewhat underwhelming? Well, I have good news.
itself
like a breathing piece of concept art. Truly, the artistic vision for this game is surreal. Wearing a gorgeous sci-fi aesthetic, every asset of the game looks like a hand-painted oil painting and is pleasantly wed to modern computer-generated particles and lighting vfx.
Breathtaking visuals. 'Nuff said.
is one of the very few games I've ever played where the audio has taken the spotlight.
Rightfully so, too, as the first thing you're welcomed with is a despondent whisper from a strange sword voiced by the talented Logan Cunningham and an ambient, upbeat tune that chillingly bears tones of alarm. It's a very harrowing start that wouldn't have been possible without the incredible audio direction.
The VO work is top of the line. With a small but carefully-selected cast, the characters are all given fantastic dialogue work. Logan Cunningham takes the forefront as the man inside the Transistor and nails his role perfectly.
The music might be my favourite aspect of the game. A 23-song OST filled with sci-fi prog, jazz and alternative rock in both instrumental and vocals flavors oozes with personality and strongly enforces the game's visual strength.
The tracks are wonderfully composed, mastered and played at the right times to exert emotion from the player. I'm still thinking of Ashley Barrett's "We All Become" everytime I think of
. I seriously recommend getting the official soundtrack to this game.

At the time of writing this, I bought this game about 24 hours ago. At the time of writing this, I also have a little over 13 hours into this game(Despite having beaten it before buying it on Steam). That alone tells you how awesome this game is, Everything from it's incredible and exciting storyline to the street vendors' dialogue is as close to perfect as I've seen.
Pros:
- The main storyline (All Sun On Yee-related missions) is like being in a really good action movie. That's the best way I can describe it. The writing, cinematography, and character development is spot-on.
- The characters is this game feel like real people. The writing and voice acting is superb. This, both fortunately and unfortunately makes it easy to get connecting to a character. You'll understand why that's a "bad" things when you play.
- The environment of Hong Kong iss so many different great things. It's gritty, dirty, vibrant, bright, dark, beautiful, etc. It's what it needs to be when that is appropriate. You never feel out of place in this game unless the game wants you to feel out of place. Also, civilian dialogue in this game is great. It acts as a comic-relief and is probably my favorite thing about this game, other than the pork buns.
- The combat in this game, both melee and armed, is great. Abviously it has a much more in-depth melee system, but the gunplay is fun and satisfying as well. I've always thought of the melee in this game as what The Batman: Arkham wanted to be. It's fluid, fun. and cool looking, but it's also challenging and requires more than button-mashing most of the time. You're also able to use several objectsin the environment like phone boothes, ovens, and hook to kill and dismember your opponents, which is just awesome.
Cons:
-This game is pretty glitchy. Not mentioning the first port of this game on PC, which literally didn't work, this game has a lot of things that look a little off. It's always something small like a floating cell phone or someone running in circles. Every once in a while you'll car will launch its self a little ways or Wei will get thrown into the air by the terrain, but I neer encountered anything that took me out of the experience.
- I wore a cop outfit this entire playthrough and, while hilarious, it's a little odd that you can do that. There were many laughs to be had when I was doing gang-activities in full police gear.Just a small thing, though. It's the outfit I chose to wear so you don't have to.
Sleeping Dogs is, for lack of a better word, fun, which is truly the most important thing any video game could ever be. It may just be a niche thing for me but it's everything I want in a video game. It's deep without taking itself too seriously. It's funny without resorting to gross-out humor or♥♥♥♥♥♥jokes. The pacing makes it fun and fair through the whole game. And most of all, the tutorials in this game aren't just boxes telling you what buttons to press. You learn through the game, which is a mark of a great game to me.

Mother russia bleeds is one of those games where your like : "Awsome concept yeah I can dig it!" But then after playing it you come to the conclusion : "Botched execution."
Oh an I already know all your pathetic little comments : "easy mode scrub lord", "git guud" etc. etc.
I've tried it on easy mode and on normal mode, with 3 AI and alone and I've come to the same conclusion everytime. This game suffers from terrible balance issues.
So whats good about it? Classic throwback to beat em ups, good art style, intresting plot, awsome tunes and when the issues aren't flaring pretty fun.
Sadly the issues flare a lot, from AI that gets stuck on a doorway to being spammed to death by enemy's that simply wont quit.
See in general I found theres 2 main classes for the enemy's you encounter (not counting bosses) you got fodder (they just throw punches n such and MIGHT have something special) and your top of the line specials (these guys do stuff like jump kicks, knockdowns, stuns, pins etc.)
The problem is the game loves to throw the later at you in ridiciouls quanity's, dogs for example are the worst their one attack is to pin you down. If there 4 dogs your entire team can get pinned! Next to that punches don't work or detect poorly on them so that just makes it worce!
Oh and don't forget what I said this is their ONLY attack, meaning their whole purpose is only to pin you down. Sorry thats not a well thought out enemy thats simply an irritating artificial difficulty curve, it's not unique it just spams to make the game seem more "difficult".
Next to dogs we got our spamming kick enemies, enemies that can stun lock combo you but worce of all enemies with guns. Now I don't mind guns but in this game theres an issue with them, 1 shot your knocked down and lose between 1/4th and 1/3 of your HP (if their handgun or ak rifle) the snipers do less but have more range etc.
Granted yes a enemy with a gun should be a priorty BUT not a cannon that can ice your whole team!
This combined with the extreem numbers that can appear on screen make this game more a pain than a fun experience.
Add to it some odd issues with hit detection IE you hitting your enemy and you have yourself a party!
As it stands I can't rate this game proper, if anything its worth a meh in my eyes. Not a no but steam wants hard values. My advice wait for fixes to come out to solve some stuff or buy on sale. I dunno how this company is with rolling out updates or such things but we will see.

This really hits the spot! I've played a lot of revival sidescrolling beat 'em ups, but I feel this one is the first that really nails the gameplay of the old classics. I'm a simple guy. I don't want to master guard cancels and air juggles to perfect a 400 hit combo. I just want to play as a muscular dude in suspenders and slam other dudes' heads into the cement really hard.
There have been games that do try to keep it mostly simple and old school, like Scott Pilgrim and Double Dragon Neon, but the gameplay just always seems a bit off. I've also played some really BAD ones like The Warriors: Street Brawl (definitely NOT to be confused with Rockstar's amazing game), and that game REALLY got it wrong. Grab attacks were severely underpowered and all enemies' attacks had priority over yours, which meant you would be huddled in a corner holding the block button hoping for an open opportunity to throw a punch. It's like these developers just watch a YouTube video of the classics without having actually played them.
This game finally gets it right. It's glorious, and I'm so grateful. The weapons feel right, the basic attacks feel good, grabbing and slamming guys with the big muscular dude is everything I could ask for. It puts a cool little spin on the health system to set it apart that I approve of. It even lets you play with bots. I give it 5 Mad Gears out of 5.

First I have to say that this is my opinion. If you feel much different from what I think then that's fine and share your thoughts below (I actually want a badge). Secondly I am only talking about the PvE (Player V.S. Environment) elements.
I have to say that this is a MMORPG I enjoyed for a while until [Spoilers?] Level 40. Then I quit because of the grinding. Especially if you level up quickly every day. Then you're pretty much done in one month (if you have much free time). I thought for a long time if I recommend this or not. But here anyway.
Pros:
The Community is nice.
The game visually looks really good.
The character customization is pretty well made. You can customize your body pretty well compared to other MMO's.
The race designs and cities are pretty great!
The sidequests are enjoyable.

Cons:

Leveling is pretty fast until level 40, WHICH IS NOT BAD but it only goes to Level 50. 60 if you have Heavensward. And completing sidequests and end-sidequests is pretty fast for me so I can actually complete this game in 1 month.

Tab-targeting slow combat, pretty standard themepark world with little interactions and forced holy trinity, so I'll go through the reasons why it's at least worth a try.
Well, first of all, while the questing system is "every WoW clone ever", it does an amazing job in keeping you invested with some impressive writing. I ended up getting hooked by the story as it went on and I still want to play to see where it will lead. There are many twists and turns and even the small optional quests have their own small story to tell. Unfortunately, the writers wanted to say a bit too much even when it's not needed so the fluff can get tiresome sometimes.
Second, the game provides instances that are linked to quests, making it mandatory to give them a go and beat them. On top of that, it's very easy to get a group for said required dungeons, even big raids as even high level players will have some reason to go through them, making the matchmaking a breeze. This is both a blessing and a curse as it makes the game feel more like a Single Player game in an MMO environment. You won't really have to depend on others to have fun as much, but at the same time there would be basically no reason to interact with other players out of dungeons.
Another thing that is interesting but kind of a hit and miss is that you can take on all classes and professions on the same character. And while you might not be interested in becoming any of the said classes, every single one of them has a storyline through class specific quests even up to the max level. The "miss" part is that there is no further customization really. While you can change a class on the fly, said class doesn't have special trees or builds for it. Can't even chose the gear really to spice it up via slightly different stats, just have to pick "the best".
On the matter of classes, the crafting and gathering classes are not the usual "no-brain-get-materials-and-craft" stuff. You are required to use certain skills and craft materials in a certain way using a mini-game. It can get tiresome as it gets longer to gain a level the higher you go, but at least it's way more interactive than the usual "go there, get this, press button, repeat" crafting and/or gathering. Unfortunately, you can't really focus on crafting and ignore fighting as you pretty much have to at least finish the story quests and all of them require fighting only.
Finally, the game is amazingly optimized. It takes a very dense city and/or fight to have the framerate drop bellow 60 on maxed out graphical settings at 1080p. While that comes at the cost of having a very instanced-based world, the fast loading times combined with the general structure of the environment nullify the issue as much as possible. There are still some times that you will get annoyed by the loading screens you have to go through, but they are not that often in my opinion.
I'd go through the issues the game has, but if you've played any other MMORPG, you probably can imagine what could be said. The world interactions and gameplay are nothing to write home about despite the developer's best attempt to make it as interesting as possible without any real attempts at creating something trully innovative and unique. But still, can't take away what's good about it, with a big amount of good free content (not requiring you to purchase DLC or expansions every update), it's hard to argue against trying it out if you have a lot of time to waste.

This is a simple top-down 2D space trading/exploration/RPG. All the basic concepts familiar to this genre are present: "jumping" from system to system to make your way across our galaxy (each system realistically aligned to our own galaxy and most having at least one or two planets with a short paragraph backstory) the option to either explore the galaxy and seek battle as a budding pirate hunter/pirate, flying the space equivalent of a ford transit van across the systems in comfy trading and occasional moments of absolute terror, or a hybrid mix. If for some reason you ever wanted to be a space bus conductor: there's passenger liners.
I tried all three initial starter-pokemon ships but settled with the transit van for my current playthrough. in this time I have: delivered a giant space-lizard amidst a pitched fight between the navies of two factions, taken a poodle half the way across the galaxy, delivered funeral documents to grieving earther relatives, and in the mean time sandwiched every bit of my hold with cargo to sell between stops. if you want something immersive to play this ticks all those boxes in even the most direly boring way to play. Picking the "interceptor" starting career immediately throws you into the slaughter.
Something over reviewers haven't covered very much here but I think is worth whetting your appetite is ship customizability: Ships are sold to you relatively complete but also have a) some empty spots and b) none of the more interesting mod cons. Take for example my light freighter I have now. I bought this thing with a loan and 500k credits to spare, why? Because I had plans. I made hull modifications that shrunk my cargo hold but gave me some more space to fit other things. in these things I fitted oversized turning thrusters and an improved shielding generator. Cooling vents/tubes were put in place of some spare bunk space, which let me switch to a beefier turret that put out just a little bit too much heat.
in the real world, I did the equivalent of buying a beat up old lorry, fitted it with armour plating and a 50.cal mounted in the passenger seat, and put a v12 where there was a v8. I now had a cargo hauler that could seriously ruin a pirate's day. you know when you watch star wars and you think "I want to have my own millenium falcon?" well now you can, and for free!
space trading games have been a personal passion of mine since I got my tiny 4-year old hands around a copy of Elite III.  It is a delight to play something that captures that essence of such games, and to do so for free is an unexpected pleasure. Thanks Mr Zahniser. I'll look out for the next thing you make!

is an isometric strategy adventure game starring Red, a voiceless entertainer and her anonymous lover, the latter trapped inside a sword-shaped tool known as the Transistor. Join Red and her mentor-turned-weapon through an epic adventure that explores the concept of singularity and discover the secrets of the city of Cloudbank and the mysterious Camerata family.
manages to take some interesting ideas and delivers them in an interesting way. Though there are a few cutscenes, most of the story is disclosed through the brief (but frequent), private whispers of the Transistor. Red happily listens, creating an authentic, naturally-developing emotional foundation between Red and her weapon.
The story arc is a little predictable and some events could have been presented in more straightforward manners.
has interesting characters and lore but a fair amount of it requires some critical thinking, assumption and the reading of hidden message terminals that share additional information about the city of Cloudbank and a mysterious event known as "The Process".
The story is overall pleasant, in large part due to the dramatic monologues of the man inside the Transistor. The game can be completed within 6 hours.
A mix of fast-paced action and turned-based strategy best describes the game's mechanics. You'll explore a large (though linear) world and frequently encounter mobs of enemies. Using dozens of unlockable Functions, you can tailor your own combat builds in very specific ways for unique effects and take them to battle.
's combat can be played in live action at full-speed or can be played in a turn-based manner by stopping time and planning attack sequences in advance. The latter is advantageous, as it allows you to use multiple moves in much quicker succession than is possible in full-speed action.
You'll be spending quite some time learning the different Functions and the different enemies and how they react to each other. When you're not fighting, you're exploring a distopian virtual city while listening to the melancholy of the man inside the Transistor.
Oh! One button is specially assigned to a singing mechanic; holding it makes Red hum to the tune of the music at any given time. Fun touch.
You know that feeling when you look at concept art for a game and think "Wow, this looks amazing!" and then the game itself looks somewhat underwhelming? Well, I have good news.
itself
like a breathing piece of concept art. Truly, the artistic vision for this game is surreal. Wearing a gorgeous sci-fi aesthetic, every asset of the game looks like a hand-painted oil painting and is pleasantly wed to modern computer-generated particles and lighting vfx.
Breathtaking visuals. 'Nuff said.
is one of the very few games I've ever played where the audio has taken the spotlight.
Rightfully so, too, as the first thing you're welcomed with is a despondent whisper from a strange sword voiced by the talented Logan Cunningham and an ambient, upbeat tune that chillingly bears tones of alarm. It's a very harrowing start that wouldn't have been possible without the incredible audio direction.
The VO work is top of the line. With a small but carefully-selected cast, the characters are all given fantastic dialogue work. Logan Cunningham takes the forefront as the man inside the Transistor and nails his role perfectly.
The music might be my favourite aspect of the game. A 23-song OST filled with sci-fi prog, jazz and alternative rock in both instrumental and vocals flavors oozes with personality and strongly enforces the game's visual strength.
The tracks are wonderfully composed, mastered and played at the right times to exert emotion from the player. I'm still thinking of Ashley Barrett's "We All Become" everytime I think of
. I seriously recommend getting the official soundtrack to this game.
I have had no technical issues with the game except for one crash after about 6 hours of continuous gameplay. This was not much of a problem thanks to the frequent autosaves. The game otherwise features PC options you'd expect and supports controllers.
delivers a full, satisfying package on all fronts from the gorgeous art style to the enchanting soundtrack to the intricate gameplay mechanics driven by a conspiracy story involving a strange family and an even stranger city.
I encourage the use of a controller. Lay back and relax. You're gonna have a good time.

A breath of fresh air. Something original that breaks away from convention. Something endlessly fun and immensely deep. Smite is all of these things.  A 3rd person Moba with various gods from religions and pantheons battling it out in various modes to establish a victor. But Smite is more than that. More than a basic MOBA, it offers more playable characters and items than you can shake a stick at and every single one has unique strengths and weaknesses to be exploited. League of Legends has such a high learning curve that it precludes many players, leaving greatness to the masters. Smite accounts for all experience, all skill levels and all levels of fun in it's battles: nobody is excluded.
This game is so easy to understand, to pick, up, to enjoy, but few can master, that it encourages all players to download and strive for greatness in the arena.
Develop your own strategy, or follow the tactics of the professionals, regardless, you will find a depth and enjoyment that few other games can match and even fewer can beat. My favourite god is Odin, what's yours?

Smite is a multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA). It involves strategy. The game is all about competition. Remember back when Call of Duty was good? That's what this game feels like now - a bunch of people fighting against each other. You will experience the same salty rage fests you did in CoD. You will also experience 2 tons of crushing force to the enemy's windpipe.
The game's competitive nature is built around how you play. Each in-game character is different, and there are over 80 of them. The game calls these characters "gods" because they are loosely based on mythological gods from various religions. Hi-Rez does a very good job at keeping all gods balanced and fair. They release frequent updates. They also release new gods sometimes. Hi-Rez will sometimes updates a god's stats so they are more balanced to accommodate for the  new base-game updates. Events occur a few times a year, allowing the player to partake in a new game mode and earn special in-game rewards.
Despite being free-to-play (F2P), Smite does not fit in the same mold as other F2P games. As a gamer who does not like F2P games, I very much enjoy Smite because their business model does not remove from the player's experience. A free player can have just as much fun as a paid player. For this reason, I purchased the
. Normally it costs $30, but I bought it on sale for $15. Buying it unlocks the full game, which means you can play as any god in the game rather than only the free ones. Don't let this discourage you, because paid gods go into a "rotation" - meaning free players can play select paid gods for the week before a new rotation starts the following week.
I have had many fun hours of Smite, and I never seem to get tired of playing. If I have persuaded you to start playing please use
. Using it will get us both in-game rewards. If you use my referral feel free to add me on Steam, and we can play together for extra in-game rewards.

I first discovered ‘Cue Club’ about twenty years, by pure chance when I was wandering about the net, looking for a good game to play – any sort of game, just something to pass a bit of time. Well, as luck would have it, one of the apps I found was this snooker game, called Cue Club, which looked mildly interesting, so I downloaded it, just to give it a go. My thoughts were, (as a regular league snooker player myself), something like, ‘I suppose this will be a bit crass and totally unlike the real game, but it might be a bit of fun for a few minutes’.
How wrong I was! Right from the very first I was impressed with the graphics employed, very realistic and with accurate reactions between the cue and the balls, just as had been claimed in the ‘splurge’ supplied; something to do with quantum math or something – it was so long ago I can’t recall the actual details. I also had complete control over things like colour of table top, type of cues and even the games themselves, because it wasn’t just snooker, but a whole list of other pool games as well. That first attempt provided me with more fun on the computer than I had enjoyed for a very long time.
As I said at the start, this all happened about twenty years ago, and I have been a ‘hooked’ player ever since, indulging several times a week, usually against the computer, but also occasionally against friends of mine, (because that’s one of the things you CAN do with this game!).
I’d always been impressed at the accuracy and realism of the game, and thought it had just about reached the limit, as far as that was concerned – until, that is Bulldog Interactive brought out the next generation, just a few months ago. This has had several improvements and alterations made to it, such as being designed to fit modern wide computer screens and better layout of game information, etc.
And so, the fun starts all over again – it’s just like having been promoted into a higher league! I would recommend anyone who enjoys snooker on the real tables, to give this game a go; I don’t think you’ll be disappointed! I should add that I have nothing whatsoever to do with Bulldog, I’m just a very happy customer who wanted to let the world know that there is fun to be had, and at a very reasonable price!
Brian Lee

I start by chastising Emily for her taste in music and calling all of her friends♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Something I probably did pretty often as a young angsty teen. She didn't seem to care that much, after all we're just sorta friends at school right?
Maybe not though because as detached as I wanted to be, the game was pretty good at letting me know that Emily and my character (CrapfaceSmokeGod) were supposed to like each other or something. Emily freaks out at me like some teenage girl (weird huh?) and makes everything my fault no matter how sycophantic I'm being. Even the neutral options lead in this direction it seems (again kind of a bummer).
So it leaves me to think about what kind of impact this game had on me. It definitely had one but maybe not the one the developer was hoping for. It's a great trip down memory lane. I recounted the girls in high school who I had blown my chances with and felt sort of bad. But then I realized they were all like Emily and felt okay. But at no point did I ever feel sad for any of the characters considering they're all pretty bad people, but hey that's what being a self centered teen is all about.
At the end of the day it's a quick fun game that serves as a vehicle for your own ♥♥♥♥♥♥ memories to come flooding back to you. I really wanted to like this game, I decided to give this one a try with the chritmas sales and I'm really glad I didn't pay more for this game. If the game still counter as early access, I wouldn't be so harsh, but the way it is the game is simply boring. The interface is anti-intuitive. The important information are in the little icons top-left of the main menu. The game grants you with somewhat useless patch note "news" from months ago. Any game played require the use of the server list, which then connects you to the game. (works but clunky) You can't access crafting menu between matches, you need to leave the server then reconnect.
So how is the game? you might ask... Well it's slow paced and everything feels a bit sluggish. I don't mean laggy, just unimpressive. You get upgrades when you kill opponents, but the upgrades don't feel like they are worth much. Everytime you die you lose the upgrades, but it never felt to me like I lost anything, nor did I ever feel like I needed to play safe so the opponent wouldn't get my "worthy" death. Played this for about 7 years now.
This is like a diablo game without having to do the grinding manually.
Instead, you send out your character on a quest using your limited energy per day, have the game running in the background and when it's done, you collect your xp/gold/whatever else dropped. Even the battles (there's one at the end of each quest for example) are automated and you can choose to skip them (they are decided by stats and some randomness - blocking, dodging, critical attacks, damage ranges etc.).
This game is pay to win. But at the same time, I'm actually not bothered by this. Let me explain. In this game, there is a currency called mushrooms. You can actually get these randomly for free, but not enough to buy all the extra energy you can each day. More energy means you can do more quests and if you can do more quests per day, you will level up and increase your attributes faster. But you also have to put more time into it. The energy you are given is enough to take a couple hours each day (of course, again, mostly having the game running in the background while doing something else), so even if I could, I definitely wouldn't spend more time than that every day. That would just burn me out.
Also, the progression of others might as well be irrelevant to you if you're not too bothered about leaderboards. There are plenty of other things to do in this game other than straight up pvp.
The other uses of mushrooms aren't all that important and don't really give much of an edge in pvp.
As a last note, there is a special "donatable" version of mushrooms, which are needed to donate to a guild. There didn't use to be, but now there is a way to get these for free as well (though the regular drops don't count). I would assume (seeing as I have over 360 of these myself), that if everyone in a guild chips in with these, this isn't an issue at all.
+ Over the years, the game received and continues to receive big updates. I'm talking entirely new features that add more and more layers of what you can actually do in this game, like the fortress (building a base, attacking other people's bases = new leaderboard entirely), pets (which you have to find first, you level them up and use to fight other people's pets), etc. Usually I'm just content doing my grinding and progressing dungeons and other stuff, but whenever one of these is announced, I'm legitimately excited.
+ You can play it on your phone (using your PC account), so that you don't miss your day's grinding if you're away or something. Or there's also the browser version, which came originally, for when you don't want your friends to know you play this and stop talking to you (jk).
+ No limits. Technically, there is a level cap (500), but I don't think anyone in the world hit that yet and it could get increased like it did once (I play on one of the oldest servers). You can increase your stats for gold to infinity, get better equipment, gems, etc. Basically, there really isn't an endgame to this. The dungeons and bosses in these are static, not randomly generated btw. and I think nobody has beaten them all yet. There's always some next challange you're looking to beat.
- P2W (see Warning section for more explanation) - you're gonna hit that top 10 pvp leaderboard only if you have more money and time than god. Even if you don't care about that, you're going to progress dungeons slower.
- This game is repetitive. Duh. Like every game about grinding. You're gonna do your set of daily chores (and by now there's a lot, but you can do them simultaneously - while questing, spin that wheel of fortune, get those arena and pet battles done etc.) and then usually be glad that's done.
